title.zh: 卷四百九十五 列傳第二百五十四 蠻夷三 撫水州 廣源州 黎洞 環州
title.en: Volume 495 Biographies 254: Man People 3: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, Li Dong, Huan Zhou
title.raw: 卷四百九十五 列傳第二百五十四 蠻夷三 撫水州 廣源州 黎洞 環州 Volume 495 Biographies 254: Man People 3: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, Li Dong, Huan Zhou

sentences.zh: 撫水州 廣源州 黎洞 環州

translations.literal: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, Li Dong, and Huan Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, the Li Dong, and Huan Zhou.

sentences.zh: 撫水州

translations.literal: Fu Shuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuizhou

sentences.zh: 撫水州在宜州南，有縣四：曰撫水，曰京水，曰多逢，曰古勞。

translations.literal: Fu Shuizhou was south of Yizhou and had four counties: Fu Shui, Jing Shui, Duo Feng, and Gu Lao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuizhou lay south of Yizhou and comprised four counties: Fu Shui, Jing Shui, Duo Feng, and Gu Lao.

sentences.zh: 唐隸黔南。

translations.literal: Under the Tang it was subordinate to Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times it fell under Qiannan administration.

sentences.zh: 其酋皆蒙姓同出，有上、中、下三房及北遐一鎮。

translations.literal: Their chiefs all bore the surname Meng and came from the same lineage; there were upper, middle, and lower branches and one garrison at Beixia.
translations.idiomatic: All their chiefs were of the Meng clan and shared common descent; the people were organized into upper, middle, and lower branches plus a garrison at Beixia.

sentences.zh: 民則有區、廖、潘、吳四姓。

translations.literal: Among the common people there were four surnames: Qu, Liao, Pan, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The commoners belonged to four clans: Qu, Liao, Pan, and Wu.

sentences.zh: 亦種水田、采魚，其保聚山險者，雖有纁田，收穀粟甚少，但以藥箭射生，取鳥獸盡，即徙他處，無羊馬、桑柘。

translations.literal: They also planted wet fields and gathered fish; those who dwelt in fortified mountain strongholds, though they had dry fields, harvested very little grain and millet, but relied on poisoned arrows to hunt game, and when birds and beasts were exhausted they moved elsewhere; they had no sheep, horses, mulberry, or catalpa.
translations.idiomatic: They also cultivated paddies and fished. Those who held mountain redoubts might have upland fields, yet harvested little grain; they lived mainly by hunting with poisoned arrows, and when game was depleted they relocated. They kept no sheep, horses, mulberry, or catalpa.

sentences.zh: 地曰帚洞，五十里至前村，川原稍平，合五百餘家，夾龍江居，種稻似湖湘。

translations.literal: There was a place called Saodong; fifty li to Qian Village the streams and plains were somewhat level, with more than five hundred households in all dwelling along both banks of the Long River and planting rice like those of Huguang and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: One district was called Saodong. Fifty li on lay Qian Village, where the river plain was relatively open: over five hundred households lined the Long River and grew rice in the manner of Huguang and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 中有樓屋戰棚，衛以竹柵，即其酋所居。

translations.literal: Within it were towered houses and fighting platforms, defended by bamboo palisades—the residence of their chief.
translations.idiomatic: There stood towered halls and fighting platforms ringed with bamboo palisades—the chief's seat.

sentences.zh: 兵器有環刀、摽牌、木弩。

translations.literal: Their weapons included ring-handled sabers, rattan shields, and wooden crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: They armed themselves with ring-handled sabers, rattan shields, and wooden crossbows.

sentences.zh: 善為藥箭，中者大叫，信宿死，得邕州藥解之即活。

translations.literal: They were skilled at making poisoned arrows; those struck would cry out loudly and die within a night and a day, but if given the antidote from Yongzhou they would live.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at poisoned arrows: the wounded would shriek and perish within two days, yet Yongzhou's antidote could still save them.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，數寇邊境，掠取民口、畜產。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi reign they repeatedly raided the borderlands, seizing people and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era they raided the frontier repeatedly, carrying off subjects and livestock.

sentences.zh: 詔書招安，補其酋蒙令地殿直，蒙令劄奉職。

translations.literal: An edict summoned them to submit; their chiefs Meng Lingdi was appointed Diandianzhizhi and Meng Lingzha Fengzhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict offering pacification and appointed the chiefs Meng Lingdi as Diandianzhizhi and Meng Lingzha as Fengzhizhi.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，又數為寇盜，止令邊臣驅逐出境。

translations.literal: During the Xianping reign they again frequently acted as bandits; the court merely ordered frontier officials to drive them beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianping they turned to raiding once more, and the court only directed frontier officials to expel them beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 其黨狡獪者凡三十餘人，宜州守將因擒送闕下，上召見詰責之，對曰：「臣等蠻陬小民，為饑寒所迫耳。」

translations.literal: More than thirty of their cunning associates were captured by the Yizhou garrison commander and sent to court; the emperor summoned and reproached them, and they replied: "We are but petty barbarians of the southern marches, driven by hunger and cold."
translations.idiomatic: The Yizhou commander seized more than thirty of their craftiest followers and sent them to court. When the emperor questioned them, they answered: "We are only humble tribesmen of the southern marches, forced to this by hunger and cold."

sentences.zh: 上顧謂左右曰：「昨不欲盡令剿絕，若縱殺戮，顧無噍類矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those beside him and said: "Yesterday I did not wish to have them all exterminated; had we indulged in slaughter, I fear there would have been none left to eat!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said: "I refused to have them wiped out entirely yesterday; had we slaughtered them all, there would have been no one left!"

sentences.zh: 因釋罪，賜錦袍、冠帶、銀彩，戒勖遣之。

translations.literal: He therefore released them from guilt, bestowed brocade robes, caps and belts, and silver trappings, admonished them, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them, granted brocade robes, caps and belts, and silver ornaments, exhorted them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 逾年，酋長蒙頂等六十五人詣闕，納器甲百七十事。

translations.literal: After more than a year, sixty-five chiefs including Meng Ding came to court and presented one hundred and seventy sets of weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, sixty-five chiefs led by Meng Ding presented themselves at court with one hundred and seventy sets of arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 又蒙漢誠、蒙虔瑋、蒙填來朝，上器甲數百及毒藥箭，誓不搔邊。

translations.literal: Meng Hancheng, Meng Qianwei, and Meng Tian also came to court, presented several hundred sets of armor and poisoned arrows, and swore not to trouble the border.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hancheng, Meng Qianwei, and Meng Tian likewise came to court, offered hundreds of suits of armor and poisoned arrows, and vowed not to molest the frontier.

sentences.zh: 比歲皆遣使來貢及輸兵器，乃授漢誠官，賜物有差，既而侵軼如故。

translations.literal: In successive years they all sent envoys to offer tribute and deliver weapons; Hancheng was then given an office and gifts in varying measure, yet afterward they raided as before.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year they sent tribute missions and delivered weapons; the court then appointed Hancheng to office and granted graded gifts, yet they soon resumed their incursions as before.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，蠻酋蒙填詣宜州自陳，願朝貢謝罪，詔守臣諭以盡還所掠民貲畜，乃從其請。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde the barbarian chief Meng Tian went to Yizhou on his own account, stating his wish to come to court in tribute and beg forgiveness; an edict ordered the local commander to instruct him that all seized people, goods, and livestock must be fully returned, and only then was his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3, the chief Meng Tian appeared at Yizhou to plead for tribute and pardon. The court directed the prefect to demand full restitution of captives and plunder before accepting his suit.

sentences.zh: 大中詳符六年，首領指揮使蒙但挈族來歸，徙於桂州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu the leader and commander Meng Dan brought his clan to submit and was relocated to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 6 the commander Meng Dan led his clan in submission and was resettled in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，數寇宜、融州界，轉運使俞獻可言：「知宜州董元己不善綏撫，昨蠻人饑，來質餱糧，公縱主者克剝概量；

translations.literal: In the ninth year they repeatedly raided the borders of Yi and Rong prefectures; the transport commissioner Yu Xianke said: "The prefect of Yizhou, Dong Yuanji, is poor at soothing and controlling them. When the barbarians were hungry and came to pawn grain for food, you allowed the granary keepers to cheat them in measuring;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they raided Yi and Rong repeatedly. Transport Commissioner Yu Xianke reported: "Prefect Dong Yuanji of Yizhou mishandles pacification. When the tribesmen came hungry to pawn grain for food, he let the granary clerks short-weight them;

sentences.zh: 及求入貢，復驟沮其意：遂使忿恚為亂。」

translations.literal: and when they sought to come to court in tribute, you again abruptly discouraged their intent—thus driving their resentment into rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: and when they sought to present tribute, he abruptly blocked them—so their anger erupted into revolt."

sentences.zh: 詔出元己，遂遣潭州都監季守睿代元己招撫，群蠻拒命，侵掠不已。

translations.literal: An edict removed Yuanji and sent Tanzhou metropolitan supervisor Ji Shourui to replace him in winning them over, but the barbarian masses refused obedience and their raids did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Yuanji and sent Tanzhou Metropolitan Supervisor Ji Shourui to pacify them in his stead, yet the tribes defied orders and kept raiding.

sentences.zh: 獻可請以本道澄海軍及募丁壯進討，乃詔益以潭州兵五千人，命東染院使、平州刺史曹克明為宜融等州都巡檢安撫使，內殿崇班王文慶、閣門祗候馬玉、內供奉官楊守珍等為都監。

translations.literal: Xianke requested that this circuit's Chenghai Army and recruited stalwarts advance to attack; an edict then added five thousand Tanzhou troops, appointed Eastern Dyeing Court envoy and Pingzhou prefect Cao Keming as overall inspector and pacifier of Yi, Rong, and related prefectures, with Inner Palace Attendant Wang Wenqing, Gatehouse Attendant Ma Yu, and Inner Palace Supply Officer Yang Shouzhen as metropolitan supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke asked to march the circuit Chenghai Army and recruited militia against them. The court added five thousand Tanzhou troops and named Cao Keming, envoy of the Eastern Dyeing Court and prefect of Pingzhou, overall pacification commissioner for Yi, Rong, and neighboring prefectures, with Wang Wenqing, Ma Yu, and Yang Shouzhen as his supervisors.

sentences.zh: 上猶以蠻夷異類，攻剽常理，不足以剿絕。

translations.literal: The emperor still regarded the barbarians as a different kind; raiding was their ordinary way and did not warrant extermination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still held that these alien tribes lived by raiding by nature and that extermination was unwarranted.

sentences.zh: 又意其道險難進師，第令克明、獻可設方略攝其酋首，索所鈔生口，因而撫之。

translations.literal: He also considered the routes perilous and troops hard to advance, and merely ordered Keming and Xianke to devise stratagems to seize their chiefs, demand the captives they had taken, and thereby pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He also judged the terrain too treacherous for a full campaign and told Keming and Xianke only to devise means to seize the chiefs, recover captives, and win them over.

sentences.zh: 克明、獻可上言：「蠻人去冬寇天河，今又鈔融州廂陽諸砦，剽劫居民，害巡檢樊明，累依宣旨詔諭，曾不悛革，臣請便宜掩擊。」

translations.literal: Keming and Xianke memorialized: "The barbarians raided Tianhe last winter; now they have again seized the stockades of Xiangyang in Rongzhou, plundered the inhabitants, and killed the inspector Fan Ming. Repeatedly, in accordance with imperial instructions, we have issued edicts to admonish them, yet they have not reformed. Your servant requests discretionary authority to strike by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: Keming and Xianke reported: "The tribes raided Tianhe last winter and now have seized Rongzhou's Xiangyang stockades, looted the people, and killed Inspector Fan Ming. Despite repeated imperial admonitions they will not reform. We ask leave to strike at discretion."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 克明乃與守珍領兵入樟嶺路，文慶、玉趨宜州西路，又令宜、桂都巡檢程化鵬取樟嶺古牢隘路會合。

translations.literal: Keming then led troops with Shouzhen into the Zhangling route; Wenqing and Yu hastened along Yizhou's western road, and Yi and Gui metropolitan inspector Cheng Huapeng was ordered to take the Zhangling Gulaopass route to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Keming marched with Shouzhen along the Zhangling road while Wenqing and Yu took Yizhou's western route; Cheng Huapeng, metropolitan inspector of Yi and Gui, was sent through the Zhangling Gulaopass to rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 化鵬遇蠻於上房兩水口，擊破之。

translations.literal: Huapeng encountered the barbarians at the two river mouths of Shangfang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Huapeng met the tribes at Shangfang's twin river mouths and routed them.

sentences.zh: 文慶、玉至如門團，為蠻所扼，不能進。

translations.literal: Wenqing and Yu reached Rumentuan but were blocked by the barbarians and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing and Yu reached Rumentuan, where the tribes barred their advance.

sentences.zh: 克明、守珍乃過橫溪恩德砦，召山獠向導，開路進師。

translations.literal: Keming and Shouzhen then passed the Ende stockade at Hengxi, summoned mountain Liao as guides, and cleared a path to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Keming and Shouzhen crossed via the Ende stockade at Hengxi, hired mountain Liao guides, and cut a path for the army.

sentences.zh: 蠻依篁竹間，時出戰鬥，輒敗走。

translations.literal: The barbarians lurked among bamboo groves, sallying out to fight from time to time but always fleeing in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes skirmished from the bamboo thickets but broke and fled whenever engaged.

sentences.zh: 旬餘，上黃泥嶺杉木隘路，溪穀險邃，蠻據要害以拒官軍，自辰至午，大潰。

translations.literal: After more than ten days they ascended the Huangniling fir-wood pass route; streams and ravines were perilously deep, and the barbarians held strategic points to resist the government army—from the hour of chen to the hour of wu they were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days they climbed the Huangniling fir-wood pass, where deep ravines let the tribes hold the heights against the imperial troops; from mid-morning to noon the enemy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其黨遂過霸苑抵帚洞，乃入中房前村。

translations.literal: Their bands then passed Bayuan and reached Saodong, then entered Zhongfang Qian Village.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitives fled through Bayuan to Saodong and into Zhongfang's Qian Village.

sentences.zh: 克明等頓兵下砦，中夕，群蠻大嘩噪，擊鉦鼓，攻砦甚急，出兵擊之，傷殺頗眾，因縱火焚其廬室積聚，自此恐懼，竄入山谷。

translations.literal: Keming and the others halted the army below the stockade; at midnight the barbarian masses raised a great clamor, struck gongs and drums, and attacked the stockade fiercely. Troops sallied and struck them, killing and wounding many; they then set fire and burned their huts and stores, whereupon from that time on, in fear, they fled into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Keming encamped below the stockade. At midnight the tribes stormed it with gongs and drums; the garrison sallied, inflicted heavy casualties, and burned their dwellings and stores, driving them in terror into the hills.

sentences.zh: 又緣龍江南岸而東，至昏暮，過石峽隘險，士不並行。

translations.literal: They again followed the south bank of the Long River eastward; by dusk they passed the perilous Stone Gorge pass, where soldiers could not march abreast.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed east along the Long River's south bank until dusk, when the narrow Stone Gorge forced them to march single file.

sentences.zh: 蠻復連弩北岸，克明遣猛士步涉與鬥，至即退走，砦於下房博賀村，克明設伏砦外。

translations.literal: The barbarians again strung crossbows on the north bank; Keming sent fierce warriors to wade across and fight—they would retreat as soon as engaged—and the barbarians encamped at Bohé Village in Xiafang; Keming set an ambush outside the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbows lined the north bank again. Keming sent picked men to ford and fight; the tribes withdrew to their camp at Xiafang's Bohé Village, where he laid an ambush outside the stockade.

sentences.zh: 其夜，蠻眾大集，遇伏發，內外合擊，追斬殆盡。

translations.literal: That night the barbarian masses gathered in force; the ambush sprang, and inner and outer forces struck together, pursuing and slaying nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: That night the tribes massed and walked into the ambush; inner and outer columns closed in and cut them down almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 乘勝搜山，悉得馬牛享士卒。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, they searched the mountains and obtained all horses and cattle to feast the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious, they scoured the hills, seized all cattle and horses, and feasted the troops.

sentences.zh: 克明等知其窮蹙，乃曉諭恩信，許以改過，於是酋帥蒙承貴等麵縛詣軍自首，克明厚加犒宴，且數責之，皆俯伏謝罪。

translations.literal: Knowing their straits, Keming and the others instructed them in grace and trust and promised forgiveness for reform; thereupon the chiefs Meng Chenggui and others came to the army with faces bound in surrender. Keming lavishly feasted and rewarded them, yet also repeatedly reproached them, and all bowed low in confession.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing them cornered, Keming offered mercy on repentance. Chiefs including Meng Chenggui came bound to surrender; he feasted them generously yet rebuked them sharply, and all prostrated themselves in apology.

sentences.zh: 及聞詔旨赦令勿殺，莫不泣下，北望稱萬歲。

translations.literal: When they heard the edict pardoning them and forbidding execution, none failed to weep; facing north they shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the edict of pardon they wept, turned north, and shouted long life to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以夷性無厭，習知朝廷多釋其罪，故急則來歸，緩則叛去，切詔克明等諭以悉還所掠漢口、資畜，即許要盟。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering the barbarians' nature insatiable and knowing they were accustomed to the court often releasing their guilt—thus coming to submit when pressed but rebelling when eased—urgently ordered Keming and the others to instruct them to return all seized Han subjects and goods and livestock, and only then permit a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged these tribes never satisfied and apt to submit only under pressure, having learned the court usually pardoned them. He urgently ordered Keming to demand full return of captives and plunder before any pact.

sentences.zh: 承貴等感悅奉詔，乃歃貓血立誓，自言奴山摧倒，龍江西流，不敢復叛。

translations.literal: Chenggui and the others, moved and pleased, obeyed the edict and swore an oath with cat's blood, declaring that if Slave Mountain should collapse and the Long River flow westward, they would still not rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Chenggui and his fellows swore on cat's blood that even if Slave Mountain fell and the Long River reversed its course, they would never rebel again.

sentences.zh: 克明等師還，宜州蠻人納器甲凡五千數，願遷處漢地者七百餘口，詔分置廣西及荊湖州軍，給以田糧。

translations.literal: When Keming's army returned, Yizhou barbarians presented five thousand sets of weapons and armor in all; more than seven hundred persons who wished to relocate to Han territory were ordered distributed among Guangxi and Jinghu circuits' garrisons and given fields and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the tribes surrendered five thousand sets of arms. Over seven hundred who wished to live under Han rule were resettled across Guangxi and Jinghu with fields and rations.

sentences.zh: 凡立功使臣將士遷補、賜齎者千八百一十六人。

translations.literal: In all, one thousand eight hundred and sixteen envoys, officers, and soldiers who had achieved merit received promotion, appointment, or gifts.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand eight hundred and sixteen officers and men who had earned merit were promoted or rewarded.

sentences.zh: 承貴因請改州縣名，以固歸順之意。

translations.literal: Chenggui thereupon requested that the prefecture and county names be changed to strengthen the intent of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui asked that the prefecture and counties be renamed to seal their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 詔以撫水州為安化州，撫水縣為歸仁縣，京水縣為長寧縣。

translations.literal: An edict changed Fu Shuizhou to Anhua Zhou, Fu Shui County to Guiren County, and Jing Shui County to Changning County.
translations.idiomatic: The court renamed Fu Shuizhou Anhua, Fu Shui County Guiren, and Jing Shui County Changning.

sentences.zh: 自是間歲朝貢，不復為邊患矣。

translations.literal: From then on they presented tribute in alternate years and were no longer a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute every other year and ceased to trouble the frontier.

sentences.zh: 獻可等又言：「殿直蒙肚知歸化州，州與撫水相接，數遣子文寶及其妻族甘堂偵軍事，又其子格與官軍鬥敵，悉部送赴闕。

translations.literal: Xianke and others also said: "Diandianzhizhi Meng Du was prefect of Guihua Zhou, which bordered Fu Shui; he repeatedly sent his son Wenbao and his wife's kin Gantang to spy on military affairs, and his son Ge fought government troops—all are to be escorted to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke further reported: "Meng Du of Guihua Zhou, which adjoins Fu Shui, repeatedly sent his son Wenbao and his wife's kinsman Gantang to spy on our forces; another son, Ge, fought imperial troops—all should be sent to court.

sentences.zh: 有蒙隻者，亦肚之子，先嘗告賊，署為昭州押牙。」

translations.literal: There was one Meng Zhi, also Du's son, who had earlier informed on bandits and was appointed Yaya of Zhaozhou."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhi, another son of Du, had earlier informed on rebels and was appointed yaya of Zhaozhou."

sentences.zh: 詔補肚密州別駕，隻海州都押牙，賦以官田。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Du Vice-Prefect of Mizhou, Zhi Chief Yaya of Haizhou, and granted them official fields.
translations.idiomatic: Du was made vice-prefect of Mizhou and Zhi chief yaya of Haizhou, with official fields granted to each.

sentences.zh: 文寶、格、甘堂並黥配登、萊州。

translations.literal: Wenbao, Ge, and Gantang were all tattooed and exiled to Deng and Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao, Ge, and Gantang were tattooed and banished to Deng and Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 寶元元年，復率眾寇融、宜州，發邵、澧、潭三州戍兵合數千人往擊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyuan they again led masses to raid Rong and Yizhou; garrison troops of Shao, Li, and Tan prefectures totaling several thousand were dispatched to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyuan 1 they raided Rong and Yizhou again; several thousand garrison troops from Shao, Li, and Tan were sent against them.

sentences.zh: 時蠻勢方熾，至殺運糧官吏。

translations.literal: At that time barbarian strength was at its height, to the point of killing grain-transport officers.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were at their strongest and even killed officers escorting grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 復詔趣兵進討，逾年乃平。

translations.literal: Another edict urged troops forward to attack; after more than a year it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a renewed offensive; more than a year passed before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，再以方物入貢。

translations.literal: During the Qingli reign they again presented local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingli they again sent local tribute.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，復至。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe they came again.
translations.idiomatic: They came again in Zhihe 2.

sentences.zh: 詔以知州蒙全會為三班奉職，又以監州姚全料為借職。

translations.literal: An edict appointed prefect Meng Quanhui Sanban Fengzhi and surveillance prefect Yao Quanliao Jiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Prefect Meng Quanhui Sanban Fengzhi and Surveillance Prefect Yao Quanliao Jiezhi.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou they came to offer tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: They presented tribute again in Jiayou 6.

sentences.zh: 是後，月赴宜州參謁及貿巨板，每歲州四管犒。

translations.literal: After this they monthly went to Yizhou to pay respects and trade great planks; each year the prefecture provided rewards in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they visited Yizhou monthly to pay respects and trade heavy timber; the prefecture gave seasonal rewards four times a year.

sentences.zh: 及三歲，聽輸所貢兵械於思立砦，以其直償之，遞以官資遷補。

translations.literal: After three years they were permitted to deliver tribute weapons to Silizhai stockade, compensated at their value, and progressively promoted in official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they could deliver tribute arms to Silizhai and receive payment in kind, advancing in rank by stages.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，知宜州錢師孟、通判曹覿擅裁損侵剝之，土人羅世念、蒙承想、蒙光仲等為亂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, Yizhou prefect Qian Shimeng and vice-prefect Cao Shi on their own authority cut, reduced, and exploited them; the natives Luo Shinan, Meng Chengxang, Meng Guangzhong, and others rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining, Prefect Qian Shimeng and Vice-Prefect Cao Shi arbitrarily cut and exploited their payments, and natives including Luo Shinan, Meng Chengxang, and Meng Guangzhong rebelled.

sentences.zh: 五年，攻德謹砦，襲將官費萬，殺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they attacked Dejin stockade, ambushed the officer Fei Wan, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year they stormed Dejin stockade, ambushed Officer Fei Wan, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 經略司問致寇狀，而宜州但以饑為言，故朝廷賜粟二萬石以安輯之。

translations.literal: The frontier commissionerate inquired into the causes of the raids, but Yizhou spoke only of famine; therefore the court granted twenty thousand shi of grain to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commissionerate investigated the cause of the revolt, yet Yizhou cited only famine; the court therefore sent twenty thousand shi of grain to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 已而守臣王奇戰死，事聞，乃詔知沅州謝麟、帶禦器械和斌經制溪洞，發在京驍騎兩營及江南、福建將兵三千五百人，以聽師期。

translations.literal: Before long the defending official Wang Qi died in battle; when the matter was reported, an edict ordered Yuanzhou prefect Xie Lin and Bearer of Imperial Armaments He Bin to oversee the stream gorges, dispatching two battalions of the capital's crack cavalry and three thousand five hundred troops from Jiangnan and Fujian, to act according to military timing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Defender Wang Qi was killed in battle. The court then ordered Yuanzhou Prefect Xie Lin and Bearer of Imperial Armaments He Bin to take charge of the stream gorges and mobilized two battalions of capital cavalry plus thirty-five hundred troops from Jiangnan and Fujian, to march as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 明年，世念等遂與諸蠻峒首領族類四千五百人出降。

translations.literal: The next year Shinan and the others, together with chiefs and clans of various barbarian stockades totaling four thousand five hundred persons, came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shinan and four thousand five hundred tribesmen from various stockade chiefs surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以世念為內殿承製，承想、光仲等十人各拜官。

translations.literal: Shinan was made Inner Palace Artisan; Chengxang, Guangzhong, and ten others each received appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan was appointed Inner Palace Artisan; Chengxang, Guangzhong, and ten others received offices.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，其酋蒙光有者復嘯聚為寇，經略司遣將官黃忱等擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning their chief Meng Guangyou again gathered followers to raid; the frontier commissionerate sent the officer Huang Chen and others to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 2 Chief Meng Guangyou rallied raiders again; Officer Huang Chen and others drove them back.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，遂以三州一鎮戶口六萬一千來上。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan they then presented registers of sixty-one thousand households from three prefectures and one garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 2 they submitted registers listing sixty-one thousand households across three prefectures and one garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔以知融州程鄰往黔南路撫諭，官吏推恩有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rongzhou prefect Cheng Lin to go to the Qiannan route to soothe and instruct them; officials and clerks received graded favors.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Rongzhou Prefect Cheng Lin to pacify them along the Qiannan route and rewarded officials in graded measure.

sentences.zh: 至和後，又有融州屬蠻大丘峒首領楊光朝請內附，又有楊克端等百三人來歸，皆納之。

translations.literal: After Zhihe, Rongzhou's dependent barbarian Daqiu stockade chief Yang Guangchao requested to submit inward, and Yang Keduan and one hundred three others came to submit—all were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhihe, Yang Guangchao of Rongzhou's Daqiu stockade sought incorporation, and Yang Keduan with one hundred three followers submitted; all were received.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻族類不一，大抵依阻山谷，並林木為居，椎髻跣足，走險如履平地。

translations.literal: The various barbarian peoples were not of one kind; generally they relied on mountain valleys for defense, dwelling among trees and forest, with topknots and bare feet, running perilous paths as if on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were diverse but generally held mountain valleys, living among the woods with topknots and bare feet, and crossing cliffs as easily as level ground.

sentences.zh: 言語侏離，衣服斒斕。

translations.literal: Their speech was disjointed and their clothing variegated.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech was hard to follow and their dress brightly patterned.

sentences.zh: 畏鬼神，喜淫祀。

translations.literal: They feared ghosts and spirits and delighted in excessive sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: They feared spirits and loved lavish rites.

sentences.zh: 刻木為契，不能相君長，以財力雄強。

translations.literal: They carved wood for contracts; they could not submit to one lord or chief, and dominance went to whoever was strong in wealth and force.
translations.idiomatic: They kept contracts on carved wood, recognized no single chief, and bowed to wealth and force.

sentences.zh: 每忿怒則推刃同氣，加兵父子間，復仇怨不顧死。

translations.literal: When angry they would turn blades on kin of the same blood, even making war between father and son; to avenge grudges they did not regard death.
translations.idiomatic: In anger they turned blades on kin, even father against son, and pursued vendettas without fear of death.

sentences.zh: 出入腰弓矢，匿草中射人，得牛酒則釋然矣。

translations.literal: Going out and in they wore bows and arrows at the waist, hid in grass to shoot people, and if given cattle and wine they would be appeased.
translations.idiomatic: They went armed with bow and quiver, shot from the grass, and could be appeased with cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 親戚比鄰，指授相賣。

translations.literal: Relatives and neighbors would point out and hand one another over for sale.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and neighbors would identify one another for sale into bondage.

sentences.zh: 父子別業，父貧則質身於子，去禽獸無幾。

translations.literal: Father and son had separate estates; if the father was poor he would pawn himself to his son—little different from beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and sons held separate property; a poor father might pledge himself to his son, scarcely above livestock.

sentences.zh: 其族鑄銅為大鼓，初成，懸庭中，置酒以召同類，爭以金銀為大釵叩鼓，去則以釵遺主人。

translations.literal: Their clans cast bronze into great drums; when first completed they hung them in the courtyard, set out wine to summon their kind, and vied to strike the drum with great hairpins of gold and silver; on leaving they left the hairpin to the host.
translations.idiomatic: Each clan cast a great bronze drum; when finished it was hung in the courtyard and wine summoned the kindred, who competed to strike it with heavy gold or silver hairpins left behind for the host.

sentences.zh: 相攻擊，鳴鼓以集眾，號有鼓者為「都老」，眾推服之。

translations.literal: When attacking one another they sounded the drum to gather the masses; whoever possessed the drum was called "Chief Elder," and the multitude submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In war they beat the drum to rally the people; its owner was styled "Chief Elder," and all obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 唐末，諸酋分據其地，自為刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tang the various chiefs divided and held the land, appointing themselves prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tang times the chiefs partitioned the region and styled themselves prefects.

sentences.zh: 宋興，始通中國，奉正朔，修職貢。

translations.literal: When the Song arose they first connected with the Central Realm, observed the correct calendar, and maintained tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: With the rise of Song they opened relations with the empire, accepted the court calendar, and paid regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 間有桀黠貪利或疆吏失於撫禦，往往聚而為寇，抄掠邊戶。

translations.literal: Occasionally when the fierce and cunning coveted profit, or frontier officials failed in soothing and control, they would often gather as bandits and plunder border households.
translations.idiomatic: When the bold grew greedy for gain or frontier officials mishandled them, they often banded together to raid border settlements.

sentences.zh: 朝廷禽獸畜之，務在羈縻，不深治也。

translations.literal: The court kept them like birds and beasts, striving only to tether and restrain them, and did not punish deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The court treated them like untamed creatures, seeking only to restrain them rather than punish harshly.

sentences.zh: 熙寧間，以章惇察訪經制蠻事，諸溪峒相繼納土，願為王民，始創城砦，比之內地。

translations.literal: During Xining, Zhang Dun was sent to inspect and oversee barbarian affairs; stream stockades successively surrendered territory, wishing to become subjects of the king, and walled stockades were first established, comparable to the inner prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xining, Zhang Dun surveyed frontier tribes; stockade after stockade surrendered land and sought subject status, and walled posts were built to match the interior.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，諸蠻復叛，朝廷方務休息，乃詔諭湖南、北及廣西路並免追討，廢堡砦，棄五溪諸郡縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou the barbarians rebelled again; the court was then bent on rest, and therefore issued edicts to Hunan, Hubei, and the Guangxi route alike to forgo pursuit, abolished fortified stockades, and abandoned the prefectures and counties of the Five Streams.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou the tribes rebelled again. The court sought repose and ordered Hunan, Hubei, and Guangxi to cease pursuit, dismantled frontier forts, and abandoned the Five Streams prefectures.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間，復議開邊，於是安化上三州及思廣諸峒蠻夷，皆願納土輸貢賦，及令廣西招納左、右江四百五十餘峒。

translations.literal: During Chongning the opening of the frontier was again debated; thereupon the three upper prefectures of Anhua and the various stream-stockade barbarians of Siguang all wished to surrender territory and pay taxes and levies, and Guangxi was ordered to win over more than four hundred fifty stockades of the Left and Right Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning the court debated reopening the frontier; the three upper Anhua prefectures and Siguang stockades offered land and taxes, and Guangxi was told to absorb over four hundred fifty Left and Right River stockades.

sentences.zh: 尋以議者言，以為招致熟蕃非便，乃詔悉廢所置州郡，復祖宗之舊焉。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on memorialists' advice that drawing in seasoned barbarians was inexpedient, an edict abolished all the established prefectures and counties and restored the institutions of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon critics argued that incorporating seasoned tribes was unwise; the court abolished the new prefectures and restored the former frontier order.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，監察御史明橐言：「湖南邊郡及二廣之地，舊置溪峒歸明官，比年浸廣其員，及諸州措置隘砦，闕人把拓，又令管押兵夫，素不習知法令，率貪婪無厭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, investigating censor Ming Nang said: "In Hunan's border prefectures and the lands of the two Guang circuits, stream-stockade Guiming officials were formerly established; in recent years their numbers have gradually expanded, and when various prefectures set up pass stockades they lacked men to hold and patrol them, yet also ordered Guanya to supervise corvée laborers—men who never properly learned statutes and ordinances and are generally greedy without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxing, Investigating Censor Ming Nang reported: "On Hunan's frontier and in the two Guang circuits, stream-stockade Guiming posts have multiplied. Pass stockades lack guards, yet local Guanya who know no law supervise corvée labor and are endlessly greedy.

sentences.zh: 況管押又皆鄉民，甚為邊患，遭困苦折辱者往往無所赴訴。

translations.literal: Moreover the Guanya are all local villagers and are a great border affliction; those who suffer hardship and humiliation often have nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: These Guanya are villagers themselves and plague the frontier; victims of their abuse often have no recourse.

sentences.zh: 議者欲俾帥臣籍其姓名，每三年一遷易，如州縣官故事。

translations.literal: Memorialists wished to have circuit commanders register their names and rotate them every three years, after the precedent of prefectural and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed that circuit commanders register them and rotate appointees every three years, as with regular officials.

sentences.zh: 或云止循舊添差，並罷管押兵夫，宜令二廣、湖南帥臣處置適宜，無啟邊禍，以害遠人。」

translations.literal: Others said merely to follow the old practice of additional appointments, abolish Guanya supervision of corvée altogether, and have the commanders of the two Guang and Hunan dispose matters suitably, not provoking border calamity to harm distant peoples."
translations.idiomatic: Others urged only the old supplementary appointments, ending Guanya control of corvée, and letting the Guang and Hunan commanders act prudently so as not to provoke frontier trouble and harm distant subjects."

sentences.zh: 詔下其議。

translations.literal: An edict forwarded the discussion for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 三年，安化蠻蒙全劍等八百人劫普議砦，火其屋宇，廣西帥臣遣縣砦將佐發兵討平之。

translations.literal: In the third year, eight hundred Anhua barbarians including Meng Quanjian raided Puyi stockade and burned its buildings; the Guangxi commander dispatched county and stockade officers and assistants to raise troops and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, eight hundred Anhua tribesmen led by Meng Quanjian raided Puyi stockade and burned it; the Guangxi commander sent local officers to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 四年，廣南東、西路宣諭明橐言：

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Guangnan Circuits Ming Nang said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Pacification Commissioner Ming Nang of Eastern and Western Guangnan reported:

sentences.zh: 平、觀二州本王口、高峰二砦，處廣右西偏，舊常無虞。

translations.literal: The two prefectures of Ping and Guan were originally the two stockades of Wangkou and Gaofeng, situated on the western fringe of broad Guang, and were formerly always free from worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ping and Guan prefectures had begun as the Wangkou and Gaofeng stockades on Guang's far western edge, long considered secure.

sentences.zh: 崇寧、大觀間，邊臣啟釁，奏請置州拓境，深入不毛，如平、從、允、孚、庭、觀、溪、馴、敘、樂、隆、兌等十有二州，屬之黔南，其官吏軍兵請給費用，悉由內郡，於是騷然，莫能支吾。

translations.literal: Between the Chongning and Daguang reign periods, frontier officials provoked conflict, memorializing to establish prefectures and expand the border, penetrating deep into barren lands—such as the twelve prefectures of Ping, Cong, Yun, Fu, Ting, Guan, Xi, Xun, Xu, Le, Long, and Dui, subordinated to Qiannan—with all requested pay and expenses for their officials, clerks, and soldiers supplied entirely by the interior prefectures; at this there was uproar, and none could cope.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning and Daguang eras, border officials stirred up trouble by proposing new prefectures to push the frontier deep into uninhabited country. They created twelve prefectures—including Ping, Cong, Yun, Fu, Ting, Guan, Xi, Xun, Xu, Le, Long, and Dui—under Qiannan, with every cost of officials, troops, and supplies borne by inland prefectures. The burden threw the region into turmoil, and the state could no longer sustain it.

sentences.zh: 政和間，朝廷始悟其非，罷之。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe period, the court at last understood the error and abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhenghe era, the court finally recognized the mistake and shut the prefectures down.

sentences.zh: 或者謂平州為西南重鎮，兼製王江、從、允等州及湖南之武岡軍、湖北之靖州、桂州之桑江峒猺，觀州則控製南丹、陸家砦、茆灘十道及白崖諸蠻，以故二州獨不廢。

translations.literal: Some said that Ping Prefecture was a great strategic fortress of the southwest, simultaneously controlling Wangjiang, Cong, Yun, and other prefectures, as well as Wugang Army in Hunan, Jing Prefecture in Hubei, and the Sangjiang-dong Yao of Gui Prefecture; Guan Prefecture controlled Nandan, the Lujia Stockade, the ten routes of Maotan, and the various tribes of Baiya—for this reason these two prefectures alone were not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Ping Prefecture was the southwest's key stronghold, keeping Wangjiang, Cong, Yun, and other prefectures in check, along with Hunan's Wugang Army, Hubei's Jing Prefecture, and the Sangjiang-dong Yao under Gui Prefecture. Guan Prefecture, they said, held sway over Nandan, Lujia Stockade, the ten passes of Maotan, and the Baiya tribes. For these reasons alone Ping and Guan were spared abolition.

sentences.zh: 臣自曆邊，即乞罷平、觀者，前後非一。

translations.literal: Since I have served on the frontier, I have petitioned to abolish Ping and Guan—not once but many times.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since my tours on the border, I have repeatedly asked that Ping and Guan be abolished.

sentences.zh: 內攝官吳芾嘗充經略司準備幹當，頗得其詳。

translations.literal: Internal adjunct official Wu Fei once served as a preparatory staff officer in the Pacification Commission and learned the situation in considerable detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fei, an internal adjunct officer who had served as a preparatory staff officer under the Pacification Commission, knew the details well.

sentences.zh: 觀州初為宜州富仁監，大觀間，帥臣王祖道欲招納文、蘭州，都巡檢劉惟忠謂得文、蘭不若取南丹之利，因誣其州莫公佞阻文、蘭不令納土，為公佞罪，惟忠遂禽殺公佞。

translations.literal: Guan Prefecture was originally the Furen Superintendency of Yizhou. During the Daguang period, the frontier commander Wang Zudao wished to win over Wen and Lan prefectures. Chief inspector Liu Weizhong said that taking Wen and Lan was not as profitable as seizing the benefits of Nandan; he therefore falsely accused that prefecture's Mo Gongning of obstructing Wen and Lan and preventing their submission of territory, convicted Gongning of a crime, and Weizhong then captured and killed Gongning.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Prefecture began as Yizhou's Furen Superintendency. In the Daguang era, frontier commander Wang Zudao sought to bring Wen and Lan prefectures into submission. Chief inspector Liu Weizhong argued that Nandan offered greater profit than Wen and Lan, so he framed Mo Gongning of that prefecture for blocking their surrender, had him convicted, and then captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 帥司奏其功，乃改南丹為觀州，命惟忠守之。

translations.literal: The commander's office reported his merit, whereupon Nandan was changed into Guan Prefecture and Weizhong was ordered to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's office reported Liu Weizhong's achievement, and Nandan was renamed Guan Prefecture with Weizhong placed in charge.

sentences.zh: 公佞之死，人以為冤。

translations.literal: Gongning's death—people regarded it as a wrongful killing.
translations.idiomatic: People widely believed Gongning had been killed unjustly.

sentences.zh: 其弟公晟結溪峒圖報復，連歲攻圍，惟忠中傷死，繼以黃璘代守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Gong Sheng rallied the stream-cave settlements to seek revenge, besieging the prefecture year after year; Weizhong died of wounds received in battle, and Huang Lin succeeded him as defender.
translations.idiomatic: Gongning's brother Gong Sheng rallied the stream-cave peoples for revenge and besieged the prefecture for years until Weizhong died of his wounds. Huang Lin then took over the defense.

sentences.zh: 璘度不能支，辭疾告罷，以岑利疆代之。

translations.literal: Lin judged that he could not hold out, pleaded illness and requested dismissal, and Cen Lijiang was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not hold the line, Lin resigned on grounds of illness, and Cen Lijiang took his place.

sentences.zh: 黃忱復建議，欲增築高峰砦於富仁監側，為觀聲援。

translations.literal: Huang Chen again proposed building up Gaofeng Stockade beside the Furen Superintendency to serve as a supporting force for Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chen again recommended fortifying Gaofeng Stockade next to the Furen Superintendency to reinforce Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷罷新邊，遂請以高峰砦為觀州，設知州一人、兵職官二人、曹官一人、指使砦保官七人，吏額五十人，廂禁軍、土丁、家丁又千餘人。

translations.literal: When the court abolished the new frontier, they then requested that Gaofeng Stockade be made Guan Prefecture, establishing one prefect, two military staff officers, one clerical officer, seven stockade and fort commanders, a clerical quota of fifty, and more than a thousand garrison troops, native levies, and household retainers besides.
translations.idiomatic: When the court scaled back the new frontier, officials asked to elevate Gaofeng Stockade to Guan Prefecture, with a full administrative staff—one prefect, two military officers, one clerical officer, seven stockade commanders, fifty clerks—and over a thousand garrison soldiers, native levies, and household retainers.

sentences.zh: 歲費錢一萬二千九百餘貫、米八千八百一十七石有奇。

translations.literal: Annual expenditure was more than twelve thousand nine hundred strings of cash and eight thousand eight hundred seventeen odd shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: It cost over 12,900 strings of cash and more than 8,817 shi of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 州無稅租戶籍，皆仰給鄰郡。

translations.literal: The prefecture had no tax-rent household registers and relied entirely on neighboring prefectures for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: With no tax-paying households on its rolls, the prefecture depended wholly on neighboring counties for its provisions.

sentences.zh: 飛挽涉險阻，或遇蠻寇設伏，陰發毒矢，中人輒死。

translations.literal: Emergency transport crossed perilous terrain; sometimes they encountered tribal raiders lying in ambush who secretly released poisoned arrows—anyone struck died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emergency convoys had to traverse dangerous country, and tribal raiders often ambushed them with poisoned arrows that killed on contact.

sentences.zh: 人畏賊，率委棄道路，縱然達州，縻費亦不可勝計。

translations.literal: People feared the bandits and generally abandoned goods along the road; even when supplies reached the prefecture, the wasted expense was beyond calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing attack, carriers often abandoned supplies along the route, and even what did arrive cost an incalculable sum in waste and loss.

sentences.zh: 昔為富仁監時，不聞有警，惟是邊吏欲以刺探為功，故時時稱警急，因以為利，遂欲存而不廢也。

translations.literal: In the past, when it was the Furen Superintendency, no alarms were heard; it was only that frontier officials wished to make reconnaissance their merit, so they repeatedly reported emergencies and thereby profited—thus they wished to preserve it and not abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: When the place was still the Furen Superintendency, there had been no trouble at all. Border officials invented alarms to claim credit for intelligence work and turn a profit, which is why they fought to keep Guan Prefecture alive.

sentences.zh: 比年戶籍日削，民多流離，或轉入溪洞，公私困弊為甚。

translations.literal: In recent years household registers daily dwindled, the people largely displaced, some turning into the stream-caves; public and private hardship was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years registered households had steadily declined as people fled, many disappearing into the hill country, leaving both government and populace in severe distress.

sentences.zh: 平州初隸融州，亦羈縻州峒也。

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture was originally subordinate to Rong Prefecture and was also a loosely controlled tribal prefecture and cave settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Prefecture originally fell under Rong Prefecture as one of the loosely governed tribal domains.

sentences.zh: 舊通湖北渠陽軍，置融江砦及文村、臨溪、潯江堡，後以地隔生蠻，遂廢。

translations.literal: Formerly it connected with Qiyang Army in Hubei, and the Rongjiang Stockade and the forts of Wencun, Linxi, and Xunjiang were established; later, because the land was cut off by raw tribes, these were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It once linked to Hubei's Qiyang Army, with Rongjiang Stockade and the Wencun, Linxi, and Xunjiang forts—but those posts were abandoned when unrestrained tribes cut the route off.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間，復隸融。

translations.literal: During the Chongning period, it was again made subordinate to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongning era it was placed back under Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王口砦地接王江，更為懷遠軍，後更為平州；

translations.literal: Wangkou Stockade, its land adjoining Wangjiang, was changed into Huaiyuan Army and later changed again into Ping Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Wangkou Stockade, bordering Wangjiang, was upgraded to Huaiyuan Army and later to Ping Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 更吉州為從州、王江為允州；

translations.literal: Jizhou was changed to Cong Prefecture and Wangjiang to Yun Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou was renamed Cong Prefecture and Wangjiang became Yun Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 並隸黔南。

translations.literal: All were made subordinate to Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: All were placed under Qiannan.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，復廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 it was abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 邊吏黃忱、李坦誑其帥臣程鄰，乞存平州，設知州一人、兵職官二人、曹官一人，縣令簿二人，提舉溪峒公事；

translations.literal: Frontier officials Huang Chen and Li Tan deceived their commander Cheng Lin, requesting that Ping Prefecture be preserved, with one prefect, two military staff officers, one clerical officer, two county magistrates and registrars, and a commissioner for stream-cave affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials Huang Chen and Li Tan misled commander Cheng Lin into petitioning to keep Ping Prefecture, with a full staff—a prefect, two military officers, one clerical officer, two county magistrates and registrars, and a commissioner for tribal affairs;

sentences.zh: 本州管界都同巡檢二人，五砦堡監官指揮十人，吏額百人，禁軍、土丁千人。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture's jurisdiction were two joint inspectors, ten commanders of the five stockades and forts, a clerical quota of one hundred, and one thousand garrison troops and native levies.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture would have two joint inspectors, ten officers commanding five stockades and forts, a hundred clerks, and a thousand garrison soldiers and native levies.

sentences.zh: 歲費錢一萬四千四百一十八貫六百文、米一萬一千一百二十五石有奇。

translations.literal: Annual expenditure was fourteen thousand four hundred eighteen strings six hundred cash and eleven thousand one hundred twenty-five odd shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Annual costs ran to 14,418 strings six hundred cash and more than 11,125 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 州無租賦戶籍，轉運司歲移桂、融、象、柳之粟以給之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had no rent and tax household registers; the transport commission each year shifted grain from Gui, Rong, Xiang, and Liu to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: With no tax base of its own, the transport commission had to ship grain annually from Gui, Rong, Xiang, and Liu to keep the prefecture supplied.

sentences.zh: 及徙融州西北金溪鄉稅米四百九十餘石隸懷遠，縻費甚於觀州。

translations.literal: Moreover, more than four hundred ninety shi of taxed grain from Jinxi Township in northwest Rong Prefecture was transferred and made subordinate to Huaiyuan; the wasted expense was even greater than that of Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When more than 490 shi of taxed grain from Jinxi Township in northwest Rong was reassigned to Huaiyuan, the drain on resources exceeded even that of Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 況守臣到任，即奏推恩其子，州、縣、砦、堡例得遷官酬賞，而稅場互市之利又為守臣邊吏所私，獨百姓有征戍轉輸之苦，誠為可憫。

translations.literal: Moreover, when defending officials took office, they at once memorialized to extend favor to their sons; prefectures, counties, stockades, and forts routinely received promotions and rewards, while the profits of tax stations and frontier trade were privately seized by defending officials and border clerks—only the common people bore the hardships of conscription, garrison duty, and transport; this was truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, new commanders immediately petitioned for honors for their sons, while prefectures, counties, stockades, and forts routinely won promotions and rewards. Tax posts and border-trade profits went to officials, leaving ordinary people to bear conscription and transport burdens—a truly lamentable state of affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜罷平、觀二州便。

translations.literal: Your subject considers it fitting to abolish the two prefectures of Ping and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: I believe abolishing Ping and Guan is the right course.

sentences.zh: 然尚有可議者，觀州初為富仁監時，有銀冶二，官取其利有常額，熙寧元降條例具在，宜先下經略司，責公晟等依熙寧條例施行。

translations.literal: Yet there is still something to discuss: when Guan Prefecture was originally the Furen Superintendency, there were two silver smelteries, and the government took their profits according to a fixed quota; the original regulations promulgated in the Yuan reign of Xining are fully preserved—it is fitting first to send orders to the Pacification Commission and charge Gong Sheng and others to implement them according to the Xining regulations.
translations.idiomatic: One point remains: when the area was still the Furen Superintendency, two silver smelteries yielded fixed profits to the state, and the original Xining-era regulations still apply. Orders should go first to the Pacification Commission directing Gong Sheng and others to enforce those rules.

sentences.zh: 況公晟實公佞弟，理宜掌州事，近雖逃歸，未為蠻族信服，察其情勢，不得不倚重中國。

translations.literal: Moreover, Gong Sheng is in fact Gongning's younger brother and by right ought to administer prefectural affairs; though he recently fled back, he has not yet won the trust of the tribes—observing his situation, he must rely heavily on China.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sheng is Gongning's brother and rightfully should govern the area. Though he recently fled home and has not yet earned tribal trust, his position leaves him no choice but to rely on the court.

sentences.zh: 若乘時授之，彼知恩出朝廷，必深感悅。

translations.literal: If at this moment he is granted office, knowing that favor comes from the court, he will surely feel deep gratitude and delight.
translations.idiomatic: If appointed now, he would recognize the favor as coming from the throne itself and respond with genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 樞密院亦上言：「廣西沿邊堡砦，昨因邊臣希賞，改建州城，侵擾蠻夷，大開邊釁。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs also submitted a memorial: "The frontier stockades and forts of Guangxi—yesterday, because frontier officials coveted rewards, they rebuilt them as prefectural cities, harassed the tribes, and greatly opened border conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs also memorialized: "Guangxi's frontier stockades and forts were upgraded to prefectural cities by officials seeking rewards. This harassed the tribes and provoked serious border conflict.

sentences.zh: 地屬徼外，租賦亦無所入，而支費煩內郡，民不堪其弊，遂皆廢罷。

translations.literal: The land lay beyond the outer frontier, rent and tax yielded nothing, yet expenses burdened the interior prefectures; the people could not endure the harm, and all were therefore abolished.
translations.idiomatic: These lands lay beyond the frontier with no tax revenue, yet inland prefectures bore the costs until the people could take no more and the posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 唯平、觀二州以帥臣所請，故存。

translations.literal: Only Ping and Guan, the two prefectures, because the frontier commander requested it, were therefore preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ping and Guan survived, kept open at the frontier commander's request.

sentences.zh: 今睹明橐所奏，利害之實昭然可見。

translations.literal: Now, seeing what Ming Nang has memorialized, the reality of benefit and harm is plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Nang's memorial now makes the costs and benefits unmistakably clear.

sentences.zh: 緣帥臣又稱公晟於南丹、觀州、寶監境上不時竊發，若廢二州，恐於緣邊事宜有所未盡。」

translations.literal: Because the frontier commander also stated that Gong Sheng on the borders of Nandan, Guan Prefecture, and the Bao Superintendency from time to time secretly raided, if the two prefectures were abolished, there would be fear that some frontier matters would not be fully settled."
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commander also reported that Gong Sheng had been raiding along the borders of Nandan, Guan, and the Bao Superintendency, so abolishing the two prefectures might leave some border concerns unresolved."

sentences.zh: 詔令廣南西路帥、漕、憲司共條具利害以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Guangnan West Route commander, transport commissioner, and surveillance commission jointly to itemize benefit and harm and report.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Guangnan West Route commander, transport commissioner, and surveillance commission to submit a joint assessment of costs and benefits.

sentences.zh: 既而諸司交言：「平、觀二州困弊已甚，有害無益，請復祖宗舊制為便。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward the various offices submitted in turn: "The two prefectures of Ping and Guan are already extremely exhausted; they do harm and no good—requesting restoration of the ancestral institutional order would be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The agencies soon agreed in separate reports: "Ping and Guan are already deeply exhausted—nothing but harm, no benefit. Restoring the old institutional order is the sensible course."

sentences.zh: 詔從其言。

translations.literal: An edict followed their words.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，詔補蒙澤進武副尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao, an edict appointed Meng Ze as Vice Commandant for Military Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 6, the court appointed Meng Ze Vice Commandant for Military Advancement.

sentences.zh: 初，宜州蠻莫才都為亂，廣西經略劉焞遣進勇副尉蒙明質賊巢，諭降才都。

translations.literal: Initially, the Yizhou tribesman Mo Caidou rebelled; Guangxi Pacification Commissioner Liu Xun sent Vice Commandant for Valiant Advancement Meng Ming to the bandit lair to persuade Caidou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Yizhou tribesman Mo Caidou had risen in rebellion. Guangxi Pacification Commissioner Liu Xun sent Vice Commandant for Valiant Advancement Meng Ming to the rebel stronghold to accept Caidou's surrender.

sentences.zh: 既而復肆猖獗，戕賊官兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again ran rampant, killing and plundering government troops.
translations.idiomatic: He soon broke out again, slaughtering government troops.

sentences.zh: 未幾，禽才都，械送經略司伏法，悉破其黨，而明亦遇害，備極慘酷，邊人憐之。

translations.literal: Before long Caidou was captured, sent in fetters to the Pacification Commission and executed according to law; his entire faction was destroyed, but Ming also met with harm, suffering extreme cruelty; frontier people pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Caidou was captured, sent in chains to the Pacification Commission, and executed; his entire faction was destroyed. Meng Ming was also killed in appalling circumstances, and frontier people mourned him.

sentences.zh: 焞乞推恩其子澤以旌死事，朝廷從之，故有是命。

translations.literal: Xun requested extending favor to his son Ze to honor death in service; the court followed this, and therefore there was this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun asked that honors be extended to Meng Ming's son Ze in recognition of his father's sacrifice, and the court agreed—hence this appointment.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十年冬，安化蠻突入內地，焚砦柵，殺居民為亂。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year of Chunxi, Anhua tribesmen suddenly entered the interior, burned stockades and palisades, killed residents, and raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chunxi 10, Anhua tribesmen burst into the interior, burning stockades and killing civilians in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宜州駐紮將官田昭明與蠻力戰敗，死之。

translations.literal: Yizhou garrison officer Tian Zhaoming fought the tribes with all his strength, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou garrison officer Tian Zhaoming fought the tribes fiercely, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，廣西路鈐轄沙世堅言：「官軍與瑤人兵器利鈍不同，宜敕沿邊軍州多置強弩毒矢，以懼瑤人。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Guangxi Route Commander Sha Shijian stated: "Government troops and the Yao people differ in the sharpness and dullness of their weapons—it is fitting to order the frontier military prefectures to deploy many strong crossbows and poisoned arrows to intimidate the Yao."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Guangxi Route Commander Sha Shijian argued: "Government troops and the Yao differ greatly in weapon quality. Frontier prefectures should be ordered to stock more heavy crossbows and poisoned arrows to deter Yao attacks."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 是年，安化蠻蒙光漸率眾抄掠，世堅討平之。

translations.literal: That year, the Anhua tribesman Meng Guangjian led his followers in raiding and plunder; Shijian suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Anhua tribesman Meng Guangjian led raids that Sha Shijian put down.

sentences.zh: 初，知宜州馬寧祖不支思立砦鹽錢，執議以為前守所積逋，止給錢一月，不能遍及蠻部，而權思立砦準備將領楊良臣復鎮撫乖方，遂致激變光漸等。

translations.literal: Initially, Yizhou prefect Ma Ningzu did not pay out the Sili Stockade salt money; he insisted in argument that it was arrears accumulated by the previous defender and paid out only one month's money, which could not reach all the tribal settlements; moreover, acting Sili Stockade preparatory officer Yang Liangchen again handled pacification improperly, and thus provoked Guangjian and others to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble began when Yizhou prefect Ma Ningzu withheld Sili Stockade salt payments, claiming they covered only one month's arrears left by his predecessor and could not reach every tribal community. Acting Sili Stockade officer Yang Liangchen also mishandled pacification, provoking Guangjian and others to rise.

sentences.zh: 詔罷良臣，貶寧祖秩，敕帥、漕以時給溪峒鹽錢。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Liangchen, reduced Ningzu's rank, and ordered the commander and transport commissioner to pay stream-cave salt money on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The court dismissed Yang Liangchen, demoted Ma Ningzu, and ordered the commander and transport commissioner to pay tribal salt subsidies on time.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，廣西漕臣胡庭直上言：「邕州之左江、永年、太平等砦，在祖宗時，以其與交阯鄰壤，實南邊藩籬重地，故置州縣，籍其丁壯，以備一旦之用，規模宏遠矣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Guangxi transport commissioner Hu Tingzhi submitted a memorial: "The Zuojiang, Yongnian, Taiping, and other stockades of Yong Prefecture—in the time of the ancestors, because they bordered Jiaozhi, were truly important barrier lands of the southern frontier; therefore prefectures and counties were established and their able-bodied men registered for use in a sudden emergency—the design was grand and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, Guangxi transport commissioner Hu Tingzhi memorialized: "Yong Prefecture's Zuojiang, Yongnian, Taiping, and other stockades were vital southern frontier barriers bordering Jiaozhi. Our ancestors established prefectures and counties there and registered able-bodied men for emergencies—a far-sighted design.

sentences.zh: 比年邊民率通交阯，以其地所產鹽雜官鹽貨之，及減易馬鹽以易銀，忽而不防，恐生邊釁，所宜禁戢。」

translations.literal: In recent years frontier people generally communicated with Jiaozhi, mixing locally produced salt with official salt to trade it, and reducing and substituting horse salt to exchange for silver; neglecting prevention, there is fear of producing border conflict—this ought to be prohibited and restrained."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years frontier people have traded freely with Jiaozhi, mixing local salt with official salt and substituting cheaper horse salt for silver. Left unchecked, this could spark border trouble and should be stopped."

sentences.zh: 既而諸司上言：「經略司初準朝旨，置馬鹽倉，貯鹽以易馬，歲給江上諸軍及御前投進，用銀鹽錦，悉與蠻互市。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the various offices submitted: "The Pacification Commission, following the original court directive, established horse-salt warehouses, storing salt to exchange for horses; each year supplies were given to the various armies along the river and to imperial tribute deliveries; using silver, salt, and brocade, all were traded with the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The agencies replied: "The Pacification Commission had set up horse-salt warehouses under court orders, storing salt to trade for horses and supplying river armies and imperial tribute. Silver, salt, and brocade were all exchanged with the tribes.

sentences.zh: 其永平砦所易交阯鹽，貨居民食，皆舊制也。

translations.literal: The Jiaozhi salt exchanged at Yongping Stockade and sold to residents for food—all were old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Trading Jiaozhi salt at Yongping Stockade for sale to local residents was long-established practice.

sentences.zh: 況邊民素與蠻夷私相貿易，官不能制。

translations.literal: Moreover, frontier people have long privately traded with the tribes, and the government cannot control it.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier people have long traded privately with tribal peoples, beyond official control.

sentences.zh: 今一切禁絕，非惟左江居民乏鹽，而蠻情亦叵測，恐致乖異也。」

translations.literal: Now to prohibit everything entirely—not only would Zuojiang residents lack salt, but tribal sentiment is also hard to fathom; there is fear of causing estrangement."
translations.idiomatic: A total ban would not only leave Zuojiang residents short of salt but also alienate the tribes in unpredictable ways."

sentences.zh: 乃牒邕州，禁民毋私販交阯鹽，以妨鈔法。

translations.literal: They then sent a dispatch to Yong Prefecture prohibiting the people from privately selling Jiaozhi salt, lest it obstruct the salt-monopoly law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then ordered Yong Prefecture to ban private sale of Jiaozhi salt so as not to undermine the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔以楊世俊襲父進通職，補承信郎。

translations.literal: That year, an edict had Yang Shijun inherit his father's Jin Tong office and appointed him Gentleman for Trustworthy Service.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court granted Yang Shijun his father's Jin Tong post and appointed him Gentleman for Trustworthy Service.

sentences.zh: 紹熙初，廣西帥以本路副總管沙世堅素有韜略，累立邊功，為群蠻所畏服，嘗破蒙光漸，示以威信，光漸不敢寇邊者累年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxi, the Guangxi commander, because this circuit's deputy commander-in-chief Sha Shijian had long possessed strategic talent, repeatedly achieved frontier merit, and was feared and respected by the various tribes—having once defeated Meng Guangjian and displayed authority and trust—Guangjian had not dared raid the border for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxi era, the Guangxi commander noted that deputy commander Sha Shijian was a proven strategist with repeated frontier victories whom the tribes both feared and respected. After defeating Meng Guangjian and establishing his authority, Guangjian had not raided the border for years.

sentences.zh: 乞以世堅兼知宜州，實能制伏蠻夷，為久遠之利。

translations.literal: He requested that Shijian concurrently serve as prefect of Yizhou, truly able to subdue the tribes—a benefit for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Shijian also be appointed prefect of Yizhou, where he could truly keep the tribes in check for lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 慶元四年，宜州蠻蒙峒、袁康等寇內地，奪官鹽為亂，廣西帥司調官兵招降之，朝廷推賞有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingyuan, the Yizhou tribesmen Meng Dong, Yuan Kang, and others raided the interior, seized official salt, and raised rebellion; the Guangxi commander's office mobilized government troops to accept their surrender, and the court granted differentiated rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 4, Yizhou tribesmen Meng Dong, Yuan Kang, and others raided the interior and seized official salt in rebellion. The Guangxi command mobilized troops to accept their surrender, and the court granted varying rewards.

sentences.zh: 嘉定三年，章戡知靜江府，建議以為廣西所部二十五郡，三方鄰溪峒，與蠻瑤、黎、蜑雜處，跳梁負固，無時無之，西南最為重地。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiading, Zhang Kan served as prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture and proposed that the twenty-five prefectures under Guangxi's jurisdiction, on three sides bordering stream-caves, lived mixed with Man, Yao, Li, and Dan peoples; insolent defiance occurred without cease—the southwest was the most important region.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 3, Zhang Kan, prefect of Jingjiang, argued that Guangxi's twenty-five prefectures bordered tribal lands on three sides, where Man, Yao, Li, and Dan peoples lived intermixed and unrest was constant—the southwest was the empire's most critical sector.

sentences.zh: 邕、欽之外，羈縻七十有二，地裏綿邈，鎮戍非一，請增置雄邊軍二百人及調憲司甲軍二百隸帥司。

translations.literal: Beyond Yong and Qin, there were seventy-two loosely controlled domains; the territory stretched vast and far, and garrisons were not one—he requested adding two hundred Border Vanguard Army troops and transferring two hundred surveillance-commission armored troops to be subordinated to the commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Yong and Qin lay seventy-two loosely governed domains across vast distances with multiple garrisons. He asked for two hundred Border Vanguard troops plus two hundred armored soldiers from the surveillance commission, all placed under the commander's office.

sentences.zh: 初，安平州李密侵鄰洞，劫掠編民，並取古甑峒，以其幼子變姓名為趙懷德知峒事，戡諭邕守推古甑一人主之。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Mi of Anping Prefecture invaded neighboring caves, plundered registered civilians, and also seized Guzeng Cave; he had his young son change his name to Zhao Huaide to administer cave affairs; Kan instructed the Yong Prefecture defender to recommend one person from Guzeng to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Mi of Anping Prefecture had raided neighboring caves, plundered registered civilians, and seized Guzeng Cave, installing his young son under the alias Zhao Huaide as cave chief. Zhang Kan urged Yong's defender to appoint a legitimate Guzeng leader instead.

sentences.zh: 十一年，臣僚復上言：「慶曆間，張方平嘗以為朝廷每備西北，孰不知瑤蠻衝突嶺外，南鄰交阯，勢須經營。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, officials again submitted: "During the Qingli period, Zhang Fangping once stated that the court always prepared against the northwest—who does not know that the Yao and Man clash beyond the mountain ranges, south neighboring Jiaozhi; the situation requires attention.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, officials memorialized again: "In the Qingli era Zhang Fangping warned that while the court always looked to the northwest, Yao and Man unrest beyond the mountains and the southern border with Jiaozhi also demanded attention.

sentences.zh: 唐時西備吐蕃，其後安南寇邊，旋致龐勳之禍。

translations.literal: In Tang times the west was prepared against Tibet; afterward Annam raided the border, and soon came the disaster of Pang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times the court focused on Tibet in the west, only for Annam to raid the frontier and trigger the Pang Xun rebellion.

sentences.zh: 國朝每憂契丹、元昊，而儂智高陷邕州，南徼騷動，天子為之旰食，豈細故哉？

translations.literal: Our dynasty constantly worried over the Khitan and Yuanhao, yet Nong Zhigao captured Yong Prefecture; the southern frontier was in turmoil, and the Son of Heaven lost his appetite over it—was this a trivial matter?
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty worried constantly about the Khitan and Yuanhao, yet Nong Zhigao took Yong Prefecture and threw the southern frontier into chaos, costing the emperor his peace of mind—is that a minor concern?

sentences.zh: 臣等比見淮甸間版築薦興，更戍日益，而廣南城隍摧圮不葺，戍兵逃亡殆盡，春秋教閱，郡無百人。

translations.literal: We have recently seen that between the Huai region fortifications and construction rise one after another and rotating garrisons grow daily, yet in Guangnan city walls crumble unrepaired, garrison troops have fled almost entirely, and at spring and autumn reviews a prefecture has fewer than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: We see constant fortification and rotating garrisons growing in the Huai region, while in Guangnan city walls crumble unrepaired, garrison troops have fled, and spring and autumn reviews turn out fewer than a hundred men per prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雖有鄉兵、義丁、土丁之名，實不足用，緩急豈能集事？

translations.literal: Although there are names such as militia, righteous levies, and native levies, in reality they are insufficient for use—in an emergency how could affairs be gathered and accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: Militia, righteous levies, and native levies exist in name only and could not meet a real crisis.

sentences.zh: 宜於嶺南要地增築城堡，籍其民兵，歲時練習，定賞罰格，以示懲勸。

translations.literal: It is fitting at key points in Lingnan to build up castles and forts, register their militia, drill them seasonally, and establish standards of reward and punishment to display deterrence and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Key points in Lingnan should be fortified, local militia registered and drilled regularly, with clear rewards and punishments to motivate defense.

sentences.zh: 如此則號令嚴明，守禦完固，民習戰鬥，可息瑤蠻侵掠之患，措四十州民於久安之域矣。」

translations.literal: Thus orders would be strict and clear, defenses complete and solid, the people practiced in combat—the affliction of Yao and Man raiding could be stilled, and the people of forty prefectures placed in a realm of lasting peace."
translations.idiomatic: With strict command, solid defenses, and a trained populace, Yao and Man raids could be ended and the people of forty prefectures brought to lasting security."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 廣源州

translations.literal: The prefecture of Guangyuan
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan Prefecture

sentences.zh: 廣源州蠻儂氏，州在邕州西南鬱江之源，地峭絕深阻，產黃金、丹砂，頗有邑居聚落。

translations.literal: The Guangyuan Prefecture tribes are the Nong clan; the prefecture lies at the source of the Yu River southwest of Yong Prefecture; the land is steep, extreme, deep, and obstructed; it produces gold and cinnabar, and has quite a few settlements and clustered villages.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan was home to the Nong tribe, at the Yu River's headwaters southwest of Yong Prefecture—rugged, remote country rich in gold and cinnabar, with scattered settlements.

sentences.zh: 俗椎髻左衽，善戰鬥，輕死好亂。

translations.literal: Their custom is topknots and left-lapped garments; they are skilled in combat, treat death lightly, and love disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They wore topknots and left-lapped robes, fought well, held life cheap, and were prone to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其先，韋氏、黃氏、周氏、儂氏為首領，互相劫掠。

translations.literal: In former times the Wei, Huang, Zhou, and Nong clans were chieftains and plundered one another.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Wei, Huang, Zhou, and Nong clans had been rival chieftains who raided one another.

sentences.zh: 唐邕管經略使徐申厚撫之，黃氏納質，而十三部二十九州之蠻皆定。

translations.literal: Tang Yongguan Pacification Commissioner Xu Shen treated them generously; the Huang clan submitted hostages, and the tribes of thirteen divisions and twenty-nine prefectures were all settled.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yongguan Pacification Commissioner Xu Shen won them over with generous treatment; the Huang clan sent hostages, and tribes across thirteen divisions and twenty-nine prefectures were pacified.

sentences.zh: 自交阯蠻據有安南，而廣源雖號邕管羈縻州，其實服役於交阯。

translations.literal: Since Jiaozhi tribes occupied Annam, although Guangyuan was nominally a loosely controlled prefecture of Yongguan, in reality it served Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiaozhi tribes seized Annam, Guangyuan remained nominally a Yongguan dependency but in practice served Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 初，有儂全福者，知儻猶州，其弟存祿知萬涯州，全福妻弟儂當道知武勒州。

translations.literal: Initially there was Nong Quanfu, who governed Tangyou Prefecture; his younger brother Cunlu governed Wanya Prefecture; Quanfu's wife's younger brother Nong Dangdao governed Wule Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At first Nong Quanfu governed Tangyou Prefecture, his brother Cunlu held Wanya, and Quanfu's brother-in-law Nong Dangdao held Wule.

sentences.zh: 一日，全福殺存祿、當道，並有其地。

translations.literal: One day Quanfu killed Cunlu and Dangdao and together possessed their lands.
translations.idiomatic: One day Quanfu killed both Cunlu and Dangdao and seized their territories.

sentences.zh: 交阯怒，舉兵執全福及其子智聰以歸。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi was enraged, raised troops, seized Quanfu and his son Zhicong, and took them back.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jiaozhi sent troops who captured Quanfu and his son Zhicong and carried them off.

sentences.zh: 其妻阿儂本左江武勒族也，轉至儻猶州，全福納之。

translations.literal: His wife A Nong was originally of the Zuojiang Wule clan; she moved to Tangyou Prefecture and Quanfu took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His wife A Nong came from the Zuojiang Wule clan; she moved to Tangyou, where Quanfu married her.

sentences.zh: 全福見執，阿儂遂嫁商人，生子名智高。

translations.literal: When Quanfu was seized, A Nong then married a merchant and bore a son named Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanfu was captured, A Nong married a merchant and bore a son named Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 智高生十三年，殺其父商人，曰：「天下豈有二父耶？」

translations.literal: When Zhigao had lived thirteen years, he killed his merchant father and said: "Under Heaven can there be two fathers?"
translations.idiomatic: At age thirteen Zhigao killed his merchant stepfather, declaring: "How can a man have two fathers?"

sentences.zh: 因冒儂姓，與其母奔雷火洞，其母又嫁特磨道儂夏卿。

translations.literal: He therefore assumed the Nong surname, fled with his mother to Leihuo Cave, and his mother again married Nong Xiaqing of Temo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Nong surname, fled with his mother to Leihuo Cave, where she remarried Nong Xiaqing of Temo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 久之，智高復與其母出據儻猶州，建國曰大曆。

translations.literal: After a long time, Zhigao again came out with his mother and occupied Tangyou Prefecture, establishing a state called Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Zhigao and his mother emerged to seize Tangyou Prefecture and proclaimed a state called Dali.

sentences.zh: 交阯攻拔儻猶州，執智高，釋其罪，使知廣源州，又以雷火、頻婆四洞及思浪州附益之。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi attacked and captured Tangyou Prefecture, seized Zhigao, released his crime, and had him govern Guangyuan Prefecture; moreover Leihuo, Pinpo, four caves, and Silang Prefecture were added to increase his domain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi captured Tangyou and Zhigao, then pardoned him and installed him as governor of Guangyuan, adding Leihuo, Pinpo, four caves, and Silang Prefecture to his domain.

sentences.zh: 居四年，內怨交阯，襲據安德州，僭稱南天國，改年景瑞。

translations.literal: After four years in office, harboring resentment within toward Jiaozhi, he raided and occupied Ande Prefecture, presumptuously styled himself the Southern Celestial Kingdom, and changed the era name to Jingrui.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, resentful of Jiaozhi, he seized Ande Prefecture, declared himself ruler of the Southern Celestial Kingdom, and adopted the era name Jingrui.

sentences.zh: 皇祐元年，寇邕州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangyou, he raided Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou 1 he attacked Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，交阯發兵討之，不克。
