translations.literal: The next year Jiaozhi dispatched troops to suppress him and could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jiaozhi sent troops against him but failed to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 廣西轉運使蕭固遣邕州指使亓贇往刺候，而贇擅發兵攻智高，為所執，因問中國虛實，贇頗為陳大略，說智高內屬。

translations.literal: Guangxi transport commissioner Xiao Gu sent Yong Prefecture commander Qi Yun to reconnoiter; but Yun on his own authority dispatched troops to attack Zhigao, was captured by him, and was therefore questioned about the strength and weakness of China; Yun largely set forth the general outline and persuaded Zhigao to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi transport commissioner Xiao Gu sent Yong Prefecture commander Qi Yun to scout the situation, but Yun unauthorizedly attacked Zhigao, was captured, and questioned about China's strength. He outlined the general situation and urged Zhigao to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 乃遣贇還，奉表請歲貢方物，未聽。

translations.literal: He then sent Yun back, presenting a memorial requesting yearly tribute of local products; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao then sent Yun back with a petition offering annual tribute, but the court did not accept.

sentences.zh: 又以馴象、金銀來獻，朝廷以其役屬交阯，拒之。

translations.literal: Again with trained elephants, gold, and silver he came to offer tribute; the court, because he was subject to and served Jiaozhi, refused him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent trained elephants, gold, and silver as tribute, but the court refused, regarding him as a vassal of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 後復齎金函書以請，知邕州陳珙上聞，不報。

translations.literal: Later he again brought a golden-casket letter to petition; Yong Prefecture prefect Chen Gong reported upward, and there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent another petition in a golden casket; Yong Prefecture prefect Chen Gong forwarded it to the court, which gave no response.

sentences.zh: 智高既不得請，又與交阯為仇，且擅山澤之利，遂招納亡命，數出敝衣易穀食，紿言洞中饑，部落離散。

translations.literal: Since Zhigao had not obtained what he petitioned for, and again was at enmity with Jiaozhi, and moreover monopolized the profits of mountains and marshes, he then recruited and accepted fugitives from justice, repeatedly taking out worn clothing to exchange for grain food, deceiving by saying the caves were hungry and the tribes were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Denied his petition and now feuding with Jiaozhi, Zhigao also controlled the mountain and marsh trade. He gathered fugitives, frequently trading tattered clothes for grain while claiming his people were starving and his tribes dispersed.

sentences.zh: 邕州信其微弱，不設備也。

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture believed him weak and slight, and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Prefecture took him at his word and kept no guard up.

sentences.zh: 乃與廣州進士黃瑋、黃師宓及其黨儂建侯、儂誌忠等日夜謀入寇。

translations.literal: He then with Guangzhou jinshi Huang Wei, Huang Shimiyu, and their associates Nong Jianhou, Nong Zhizhong, and others day and night plotted to invade.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted night and day with Guangzhou degree holders Huang Wei and Huang Shimiyu, along with followers Nong Jianhou and Nong Zhizhong, to launch an invasion.

sentences.zh: 一夕，焚其巢穴，紿其眾曰：「平生積聚，今為天火焚，無以為生，計窮矣。

translations.literal: One evening, he burned his nest-cave, deceiving his masses saying: "Our lifelong accumulations—now burned by heaven's fire—we have no means to live; our plans are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: One night he set fire to his own stronghold and lied to his followers: "Everything we saved has been destroyed by heaven's fire. We cannot survive—our options are gone.

sentences.zh: 當拔邕州，據廣州以自王，否則必死。」

translations.literal: We ought to capture Yong Prefecture, seize Guangzhou to make ourselves kings—or we will surely die."
translations.idiomatic: We must take Yong Prefecture, hold Guangzhou, and declare ourselves kings—or we are dead."

sentences.zh: 四年四月，率眾五千沿鬱江東下，攻破橫山砦，遂破邕州，執知州陳珙等，兵死千餘人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, leading a host of five thousand along the Yu River eastward, he attacked and broke Hengshan Stockade, then broke Yong Prefecture, seized prefect Chen Gong and others; more than a thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, he led five thousand men down the Yu River, overran Hengshan Stockade and Yong Prefecture, captured Prefect Chen Gong, and killed more than a thousand defenders.

sentences.zh: 智高閱軍資庫，得所上金、函，怒謂珙曰：「我求一官統攝諸部，汝不以聞，何也？」

translations.literal: Zhigao inspected the military supplies storehouse, obtained the submitted gold and casket, angrily said to Gong: "I sought one office to command and oversee the various tribes—you did not report it to the court. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Searching the arsenal, Zhigao found Chen Gong's unreported petition in its golden casket and raged: "I asked for authority over all the tribes—why didn't you tell the court?"

sentences.zh: 珙對：「嘗奏，不報。」

translations.literal: Gong replied: "I once memorialized; there was no response."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong answered, "I did report it—the court never replied."

sentences.zh: 索奏草不獲，遂扶珙出，珙惶恐呼萬歲，救自效，不聽，乃並其屬及廣西都監張立害之。

translations.literal: Demanding the memorial draft and not obtaining it, he then supported Gong out; Gong in panic called "Long live!", offering to serve in redemption—they did not listen, and then together with his subordinates and Guangxi chief inspector Zhang Li harmed them.
translations.idiomatic: When no draft could be found, Zhigao dragged Chen Gong out. Gong cried "Long live the Emperor!" and offered to serve, but was ignored. Zhigao killed him, his staff, and Guangxi chief inspector Zhang Li.

sentences.zh: 立臨刑大罵，不為屈。

translations.literal: Li at the execution cursed loudly, and was not made to bend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li cursed Zhigao to the end and never yielded.

sentences.zh: 於是智高僭號仁惠皇帝，改年啟曆，赦境內。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhigao arrogated the title Emperor Renhui, changed the era to Qili, and pardoned within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao then proclaimed himself Emperor Renhui, named his era Qili, and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 師宓以下皆稱中國官名。

translations.literal: Shimiyu and those below all took Chinese court official titles.
translations.idiomatic: Shimiyu and the others all adopted titles from the imperial bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下久安，嶺南州縣無備，一旦兵起倉卒，不知所為，守將多棄城遁。

translations.literal: At this time, the realm had long been at peace; Lingnan prefectures and counties had no preparedness. Suddenly troops rose in haste, not knowing what to do—the defending generals mostly abandoned cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had been at peace for years, and Lingnan had no defenses. When rebellion erupted overnight, local commanders panicked and many fled their posts.

sentences.zh: 故智高所向得志，相繼破橫、貴、龔、潯、藤、梧、封、康、端九州，害曹覲於封州、趙師旦馬貴於康州，餘殺官吏甚眾。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever Zhigao went he got his wish; in succession he broke the nine prefectures of Heng, Gui, Gong, Xun, Teng, Wu, Feng, Kang, and Duan, killed Cao Jin at Feng Prefecture and Zhao Shidan and Ma Gui at Kang Prefecture; besides these he killed very many officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao swept through Heng, Gui, Gong, Xun, Teng, Wu, Feng, Kang, and Duan, killing Cao Jin at Fengzhou and Zhao Shidan and Ma Gui at Kangzhou along with countless other officials.

sentences.zh: 所過焚府庫，進圍廣州。

translations.literal: Where he passed he burned government storehouses, advancing to besiege Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His army burned treasuries along the way and pushed on to besiege Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，智高將至，守將仲簡不許民入保城中，民不得入者皆附智高，智高勢益張。

translations.literal: Initially, as Zhigao was about to arrive, the defending general Zhong Jian did not permit the people to enter and take refuge within the city; those who could not enter all attached to Zhigao, and Zhigao's power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao approached, Defender Zhong Jian refused to let civilians into the city. Those left outside joined the rebels, and Zhigao's forces swelled.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏瓘築州城，鑿井畜水，作大弩為守備。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Guan had built the prefectural city wall, dug wells to store water, and made large crossbows for defensive preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Guan had fortified the city with walls, wells, and giant crossbows.

sentences.zh: 至是，智高為雲梯土山，攻城甚急，又斷流水，而城堅，井飲不竭，弩發，中輒洞潰，智高力屈。

translations.literal: At this time, Zhigao made cloud-ladders and earthen mounds, attacking the city very urgently; he also cut off the flowing water, but the walls were strong, well water for drinking did not run dry, crossbows fired, and hits immediately pierced through and burst; Zhigao's strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao built siege towers and ramparts and cut off the water supply, but the walls held, the wells never ran dry, and Wei Guan's crossbows punched clean holes through his ranks until Zhigao's army was spent.

sentences.zh: 會知英州蘇緘屯兵邊渡村，扼其歸路；

translations.literal: It happened that Ying Prefecture prefect Su Jian stationed troops at Biandu Village, blocking his route of return;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yingzhou Prefect Su Jian blocked the retreat at Biandu Village;

sentences.zh: 番禺縣令蕭注募土丁及海上強壯二千餘人，與智高眾格鬥，焚其戰艦；

translations.literal: Panyu county magistrate Xiao Zhu recruited more than two thousand local militia and strong men from the sea, grappled with Zhigao's masses, and burned his warships;
translations.idiomatic: Panyu Magistrate Xiao Zhu rallied over two thousand local militiamen and sailors, fought Zhigao's troops, and burned his fleet;

sentences.zh: 轉運使王罕亦自外至，益修守備。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Wang Han also arrived from outside, further repairing defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Wang Han arrived from outside and tightened the defenses.

sentences.zh: 智高知不可拔，圍五十七日，七月壬戌，解去。

translations.literal: Zhigao knew it could not be taken; he besieged for fifty-seven days; on the renxu day of the seventh month, he lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: After fifty-seven days, seeing Guangzhou could not be taken, Zhigao withdrew on the renxu day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 由清遠濟江，擁婦女作樂而行，遇張忠戰於白田，忠死之。

translations.literal: By Qingyuan he crossed the river, embracing women and making music as he went; he encountered Zhang Zhong and fought at Baitian; Zhong died in it.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river near Qingyuan, marching to music with captive women until Zhang Zhong intercepted him at Baitian and was killed.

sentences.zh: 去攻賀州，不克，夜害蔣偕於太平場。

translations.literal: He went on to attack He Prefecture, did not overcome it; at night he harmed Jiang Xie at Taiping Ground.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to take Hezhou, he ambushed and killed Jiang Xie at Taiping that night.

sentences.zh: 九月庚申，破昭州，害王正倫等於館門驛。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the ninth month, he broke Zhao Prefecture, harming Wang Zhenglun and others at Guanmen Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the ninth month he seized Zhaozhou and murdered Wang Zhenglun and others at Guanmen Post Station.

sentences.zh: 州之山有數穴，大可容數百千人，民聞兵至，走匿其中，智高知之，縱火，皆焚死。

translations.literal: The prefecture's mountains had several caves, large enough to hold several hundred or thousand people; when the people heard troops arrive, they ran and hid within them; Zhigao knew this, set fire, and all were burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Locals fled into mountain caves that could shelter thousands. Zhigao found them and set the caves ablaze, burning everyone inside.

sentences.zh: 十月丁丑，破賓州。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day of the tenth month, he broke Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the tenth month he captured Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，復據邕州，日夜伐木治舟楫，揚言復趨廣州。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day, he again occupied Yong Prefecture, day and night felling trees to build boats and oars, proclaiming he would again rush toward Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day he retook Yongzhou, cutting timber day and night to build boats while boasting he would strike Guangzhou again.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬申，又敗陳曙於金城驛。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the twelfth month, he again defeated Chen Shu at Jincheng Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the twelfth month he routed Chen Shu at Jincheng Post Station.

sentences.zh: 初，智高以反聞，朝廷命曙就擊之，既而楊畋、曹修、張忠、蔣偕相繼出，又以余靖、孫沔為安撫使。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhigao by false intelligence misled the court to order Shu to go and strike him; afterward Yang Tian, Cao Xiu, Zhang Zhong, and Jiang Xie successively went out; again Yu Jing and Sun Mian were made pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao's disinformation first drew Chen Shu, then Yang Tian, Cao Xiu, Zhang Zhong, and Jiang Xie; the court also appointed Yu Jing and Sun Mian as pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 畋、修聞智高至，退軍避之。

translations.literal: Tian and Xiu, hearing Zhigao had arrived, withdrew their armies to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tian and Cao Xiu retreated as soon as they heard Zhigao was near.

sentences.zh: 忠、偕勇而無謀，皆死。

translations.literal: Zhong and Xie were brave but without strategy; both died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong and Jiang Xie fought boldly but recklessly, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 智高益自恣，南土騷然。

translations.literal: Zhigao grew ever more self-indulgent; the southern lands were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao grew bolder still, and the south was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以為憂，命狄青為宣撫使，諸將皆受青節制。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong regarded it as a worry, and ordered Di Qing as pacification commissioner; all generals were under Qing's command and control.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Emperor Renzong put Di Qing in overall command, with every general under his authority.

sentences.zh: 曙恐青至有功，亟挑戰，故敗。

translations.literal: Shu feared that when Qing arrived there would be merit, and urgently challenged battle; therefore he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu, afraid Di Qing would win the glory, rashly offered battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，青及沔、靖會兵賓州，官軍、土丁合三萬一千餘人，按軍法誅曙及指揮使袁用等三十二人於坐，一軍大振。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Qing together with Mian and Jing joined forces at Bin Prefecture; regular army and local militia totaled more than thirty-one thousand; according to military law he executed Shu and commanders Yuan Yong and thirty-two others on the spot; the whole army was greatly invigorated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Di Qing, Sun Mian, and Yu Jing mustered over thirty-one thousand troops at Binzhou and, enforcing military law, executed Chen Shu, Commander Yuan Yong, and thirty others on the spot. Morale soared.

sentences.zh: 於是進兵，青將前陣，沔將次陣，靖將後陣，以一晝夜絕昆侖關歸仁鋪。

translations.literal: Thereupon they advanced troops; Qing commanded the front formation, Mian the second formation, Jing the rear formation; in one day and night they crossed Kunlun Pass to Guiren Station.
translations.idiomatic: They marched forward with Di Qing leading the vanguard, Sun Mian the center, and Yu Jing the rear, crossing Kunlun Pass to Guiren Station in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 智高聞王師絕險而至，出其不意，悉眾來拒，執大盾、摽槍，衣絳衣，望之如火，青陣少卻，先鋒孫節死之。

translations.literal: Zhigao heard the imperial army had crossed dangerous passes and arrived, taking him unawares; he mustered all his forces to resist, holding large shields and javelin lances, wearing crimson clothing—looking at them was like fire; Qing's formation slightly retreated; vanguard Sun Jie died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Surprised that imperial troops had crossed Kunlun Pass, Zhigao marched out his entire force with great shields and crimson spears like a wall of fire. Di Qing's line buckled briefly and vanguard Sun Jie was killed.

sentences.zh: 青起麾蕃落騎兵，張在左翼出其後交擊，左者右，右者左，已而左者復左，右者復右，其眾不知所為，大敗走。

translations.literal: Qing rose and waved the frontier tribal cavalry; deployed on the left flank he struck from behind in mutual attack; those on the left went right, those on the right went left; then those on the left again went left, those on the right again went right; his masses did not know what to do, and were greatly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing then unleashed tribal cavalry on the left, wheeling them behind the enemy and feinting left and right until the rebels lost all sense of direction and broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，智高復趨邕州，夜焚城遁，由合江口入大理國。

translations.literal: It happened to be sunset; Zhigao again rushed toward Yong Prefecture, burned the city by night and fled, entering the Dali kingdom by Hejiang Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Zhigao fled back toward Yongzhou, burned the city overnight, and escaped into Dali through Hejiangkou.

sentences.zh: 得屍五千三百四十一，築為京觀，所掠生口萬餘人，復其業。

translations.literal: They obtained corpses numbering five thousand three hundred forty-one, built them into a jingguan mound; captives taken numbered more than ten thousand people—they restored their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: They counted 5,341 enemy dead and erected a victory mound; more than ten thousand captives were freed to resume their lives.

sentences.zh: 獲偽印九，黃師宓而下偽官五十七人，梟其首城上，收馬牛、金帛以钜萬計。

translations.literal: They obtained nine false seals; from Huang Shimiyu downward, fifty-seven false officials; their heads were displayed on the city wall; horses, cattle, gold, and silk collected numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Nine rebel seals and fifty-seven officials down to Huang Shimiyu were captured; their heads were hung on the city wall. Booty in horses, cattle, gold, and silk amounted to vast sums.

sentences.zh: 智高自起兵幾一年，暴踐一方，如行無人之境，吏民不勝其毒。

translations.literal: From Zhigao's raising troops it was nearly one year; he violently trampled one region, as if marching through land with no people; officials and people could not bear his poison.
translations.idiomatic: In nearly a year of rebellion Zhigao had ravaged the region as if no one stood in his way, until officials and commoners alike could bear no more.

sentences.zh: 朝廷為下赦令，優除復，慰拊瘡痍，百姓始得更生雲。

translations.literal: The court issued pardoning edicts, preferential exemptions and restoration, comforting the wounded; the common people at last could live again.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued amnesties, tax relief, and relief for the wounded, and the people could at last begin to rebuild their lives.

sentences.zh: 先是，謠言「農家種，糴家收。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a saying circulated: "The Nong family plants, the Di family harvests."
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy had circulated: "The Nong clan sows, the Di clan reaps."

sentences.zh: 已而智高叛，為青破，皆如其謠。

translations.literal: Later Zhigao rebelled and was broken by Qing—all came about as the saying said.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao rebelled and was crushed by Di Qing, events unfolded exactly as the prophecy foretold.

sentences.zh: 智高母阿儂有計謀，智高攻陷城邑，多用其策，僭號皇太后，性慘毒，嗜小兒肉，每食必殺小兒。

translations.literal: Zhigao's mother A Nong had stratagems; when Zhigao attacked and captured cities and towns, he often used her plans; she arrogated the title Empress Dowager; her nature was cruel and poisonous; she doted on child flesh; every meal she must kill a child.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao's mother A Nong was the strategist behind many of his conquests. He proclaimed her Empress Dowager. Cruel by nature, she ate human flesh and demanded a child killed for every meal.

sentences.zh: 智高敗走，阿儂入保特磨，依其夫儂夏卿，收殘眾得三千餘人，習騎戰，復欲入寇。

translations.literal: Zhigao was defeated and fled; A Nong entered and held Temo, relying on her husband Nong Xiaqing; she gathered remnant forces totaling more than three thousand, practiced mounted combat, and again wished to invade.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhigao's defeat A Nong fortified Temo with her husband Nong Xiaqing, rallied three thousand survivors, trained cavalry, and planned another raid.

sentences.zh: 至和初，余靖督部吏黃汾黃獻珪石鑒、進士吳舜舉發峒兵入特磨，掩襲之，獲阿儂及智高弟智光、子繼宗繼封，檻至京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhihe, Yu Jing supervised department clerks Huang Fen, Huang Xiangui, and Shi Jian, and jinshi Wu Shunju, dispatching cave militia into Temo for a surprise attack; they captured A Nong and Zhigao's younger brother Zhiguang and sons Jizong and Jifeng, caged to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhihe era Yu Jing sent cave militia led by Huang Fen, Huang Xiangui, Shi Jian, and Wu Shunju into Temo in a surprise raid, capturing A Nong, Zhigao's brother Zhiguang, and sons Jizong and Jifeng and sending them to the capital in cages.

sentences.zh: 初未欲殺，日給食飲，欲以誘出智高，或傳智高死，乃悉棄市。

translations.literal: Initially they did not wish to kill them; daily they supplied food and drink, wishing thereby to lure Zhigao out; when some reported Zhigao was dead, then all were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court kept them alive on daily rations hoping to lure Zhigao out. When rumors spread that he was dead, all were executed.

sentences.zh: 既而西川復奏智高未死，謀寇黎、雅州，詔本路為備。

translations.literal: Afterward Xichuan again reported that Zhigao was not dead and plotted to raid Li and Ya prefectures; an edict ordered that circuit to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sichuan reported that Zhigao was still alive and planning raids on Lizhou and Yazhou, and the court ordered the circuit to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞孫抃又請敕益州先事經制，以安蜀人。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Sun Bian again requested an imperial command that Yizhou take preventive measures in advance, to settle the Shu people.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Sun Bian also urged the court to order Yizhou to take preemptive measures to reassure the people of Shu.

sentences.zh: 然智高卒不出，其存亡莫可知也。

translations.literal: Yet Zhigao in the end did not emerge; whether he lived or died could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao never reappeared, and his fate remained unknown.

sentences.zh: 儂氏又有宗旦者，知雷火洞，稍桀黠。

translations.literal: Among the Nong clan there was also Zongdan, who controlled Leihuo Cave and was somewhat fierce and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Another Nong clansman, Zongdan, controlled Leihuo Cave and had grown restive and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，嘗入寇，知桂州蕭固招之內屬，以為忠武將軍，又補其子知溫悶峒日新為三班奉職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, he once invaded; Guilin prefect Xiao Gu recruited him to submit internally, appointing him Loyal and Martial General; again appointing his sons Zhiwen and Mendong Rixin as Third-Rank Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: After raiding in Jiayou 2, Guilin Prefect Xiao Gu induced Zongdan to submit and made him Loyal and Martial General, with sons Zhiwen and Mendong Rixin given court posts.

sentences.zh: 七年，宗旦父子請以所領雷火、計城諸峒屬縣官，願得歸樂州，永為王民。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Zongdan father and son requested that the Leihuo, Jicheng, and various caves they led be placed under county officials, wishing to reside in Le Prefecture, forever as the king's people.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Zongdan and his sons asked to place Leihuo, Jicheng, and their other cave domains under county administration and relocate to Le Prefecture as permanent subjects of the empire.

sentences.zh: 詔各遷一官，以宗旦知順安州，仍賜耕牛、鹽彩。

translations.literal: An edict promoted each one rank; Zongdan was made prefect of Shun'an Prefecture, and still granted plow oxen, salt, and colored cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted each a rank, made Zongdan prefect of Shun'an, and granted plow oxen, salt, and colored cloth.

sentences.zh: 是歲，儂夏卿、儂平、儂亮亦自特磨來歸，皆其族也。

translations.literal: That year, Nong Xiaqing, Nong Ping, and Nong Liang also came from Temo to submit—all were of their clan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Nong Xiaqing, Nong Ping, and Nong Liang also came in from Temo—all members of the clan.

sentences.zh: 日新後嘗監邕州稅。

translations.literal: Rixin later once supervised Yong Prefecture taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Rixin later served as overseer of Yongzhou taxes.

sentences.zh: 治平中，宗旦與交阯李日尊、劉紀有隙，畏逼，知桂州陸詵因使人說之，遂棄其州內徙，命為右千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era, Zongdan had a rift with Jiaozhi's Li Rizun and Liu Ji, feared pressure; Guilin prefect Lu Shen therefore sent men to persuade him; he then abandoned his prefecture and moved internally, and was appointed Right Qianniu Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiping era, feuding with Jiaozhi's Li Rizun and Liu Ji, Zongdan was persuaded by Guilin Prefect Lu Shen to abandon his domain and move inland, receiving appointment as Right Qianniu Guard General.

sentences.zh: 有甲峒蠻者，亦役屬交阯，間出寇邕州。

translations.literal: There were Jia Cave barbarians who also served as subjects of Jiaozhi, intermittently coming out to raid Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Jia Cave tribes, vassals of Jiaozhi, sometimes raided Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，嘗掠思陵州憑祥峒生口，殺登龍鎮將而去。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou, they once plundered Siling Prefecture's Pingxiang Cave for captives, killed the Denglong garrison commander, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 3 they raided Pingxiang Cave in Siling Prefecture for captives, killed the Denglong garrison commander, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐五年，合交阯、門州等蠻五千餘人復為寇，與官兵拒戰，斬首數百。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiayou, combining with Jiaozhi, Men Prefecture, and other barbarians totaling more than five thousand, they again raided; fighting resisting official troops, several hundred heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 5 they joined with over five thousand men from Jiaozhi, Menzhou, and allied tribes to raid again; government forces fought them and took several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 詔知桂州蕭固趨邕州發諸郡兵，與轉運使宋咸、提點刑獄李師中合議追討。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guilin prefect Xiao Gu to hurry to Yong Prefecture and dispatch troops from the various prefectures; together with transport commissioner Song Xian and judicial intendant Li Shizhong he jointly deliberated pursuit and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Guilin Prefect Xiao Gu to rush to Yongzhou, mobilize troops from surrounding prefectures, and pursue the raiders with Transport Commissioner Song Xian and Judicial Intendant Li Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 是歲數入寇，又詔安撫使余靖擊之。

translations.literal: That year they entered to raid several times; again an edict ordered pacification commissioner Yu Jing to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: They raided repeatedly that year, and Pacification Commissioner Yu Jing was ordered to attack them.

sentences.zh: 蘇茂州蠻亦近邕州，至和、嘉祐中，皆嘗擾邊。

translations.literal: Sumo Prefecture barbarians also were near Yong Prefecture; during Zhihe and Jiayou, all once disturbed the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Sumo Prefecture tribes near Yongzhou also harassed the frontier during the Zhihe and Jiayou eras.

sentences.zh: 黎洞，唐故瓊管之地，在大海南，距雷州泛海一日而至。

translations.literal: Li Cave was the former Qiong-administration territory of Tang, south of the great sea; from Le Prefecture by sea one day's voyage would reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cave lay in what had been Tang's Qiong administration, south of the sea a day's sail from Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 其地有黎母山，黎人居焉。

translations.literal: That land had Limu Mountain; Li people dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: The region centered on Limu Mountain, home to the Li people.

sentences.zh: 舊說五嶺之南，人雜夷獠，朱崖環海，豪富兼並，役屬貧弱；

translations.literal: Old accounts say south of the Five Ridges, people mixed with Yi and Liao, Zhuya encircled by sea; the rich and powerful annexed and merged, enslaving and subjecting the poor and weak;
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that south of the Five Ridges peoples mingled with tribal groups; on sea-girt Hainan the wealthy absorbed the poor and reduced them to servitude;

sentences.zh: 婦人服緦緶，績木皮為布，陶土為釜，器用瓠瓢；

translations.literal: Women wore ramie and cotton cloth, spun tree bark into cloth, fired clay into cauldrons, and used gourd ladles as utensils;
translations.idiomatic: Women wore hemp and cotton, wove cloth from tree bark, fired clay pots, and used gourd vessels;

sentences.zh: 人飲石汁，又有椒酒，以安石榴花著甕中即成酒。

translations.literal: People drank stone juice; there was also pepper wine—placing pomegranate flowers in a jar would make wine.
translations.idiomatic: They drank a mineral spring liquor and a pepper wine made by steeping pomegranate blossoms in jars.

sentences.zh: 俗呼山嶺為「黎」，居其間者號曰黎人，弓刀未嘗去手。

translations.literal: Custom calls mountain ridges "Li"; those dwelling among them were styled Li people; bow and knife never left their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains were called "Li," and those who lived among them were known as the Li people, who never went unarmed.

sentences.zh: 弓以竹為弦。

translations.literal: Bows used bamboo as strings.
translations.idiomatic: Their bows were strung with bamboo.

sentences.zh: 今儋崖、萬安皆與黎為境，其服屬州縣者為熟黎，其居山洞無征徭者為生黎，時出與郡人互市。

translations.literal: Now Dan Cliff and Wan'an all bordered the Li; those who submitted and were subject to prefectures and counties were "ripe Li"; those dwelling in mountain caves without tax and corvée were "raw Li"; they sometimes came out to trade with the prefecture people.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhou, Yazhou, and Wan'an all bordered Li territory. Those under county authority were called "acculturated Li"; those in mountain caves free of taxes and labor service were "wild Li," who sometimes came down to trade with Han settlers.

sentences.zh: 至和初，有黎人符護者，邊吏嘗獲其奴婢十人，還之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhihe, there was a Li man named Fu Hu; frontier officials once captured ten of his male and female servants and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhihe era a Li leader named Fu Hu had ten servants seized by border officials, who later returned them.

sentences.zh: 符護亦嘗犯邊，執瓊、崖州巡檢慕容允則及軍士，至是，以軍士五十六人與允則來歸。

translations.literal: Fu Hu also once violated the border, seizing Qiong and Ya prefectures' patrol inspector Murong Yunze and soldiers; at this time, with fifty-six soldiers and Yunze, he came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hu had also raided the frontier and captured Patrol Inspector Murong Yunze of Qiong and Yazhou along with his men; now he returned with Yunze and fifty-six soldiers.

sentences.zh: 允則道病死，詔軍士至者貸其罪。

translations.literal: Yunze died of illness on the road; an edict pardoned the crimes of the soldiers who arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yunze died on the journey home, and the court pardoned the returned soldiers.

sentences.zh: 嘉定九年五月，詔宜人王氏女吳氏襲封，統領三十六峒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year of Jiading, an edict had Lady Wang's daughter Lady Wu inherit enfeoffment, commanding thirty-six caves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jiading 9, Lady Wu, daughter of Lady Wang, was enfeoffed to command thirty-six caves.

sentences.zh: 環州蠻區氏，州隸宜州羈縻，領思恩、都亳二縣。

translations.literal: Huan Prefecture barbarians of the Qu clan—the prefecture was subordinate to Yizhou as a jimi dependency, administering the two counties of Si'en and Dumei.
translations.idiomatic: The Qu clan of Huan Prefecture, a jimi dependency under Yizhou, governed Si'en and Dumei counties.

sentences.zh: 有區希範者，思恩人也。

translations.literal: There was a Qu Xifan, a man of Si'en.
translations.idiomatic: One of them was Qu Xifan of Si'en.

sentences.zh: 狡黠頗知書，嘗舉進士，試禮部。

translations.literal: Cunning and shrewd, he was quite literate; he once passed the jinshi examination and tested at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and literate, he had taken the jinshi examination at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 景祐五年，與其叔正辭應募，從官軍討安化州叛蠻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingyou, he and his uncle Zhengchen answered recruitment, following official troops to suppress Anhua Prefecture's rebellious barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 5 he and his uncle Zhengchen enlisted and joined government forces against rebel tribes in Anhua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而希範擊登聞鼓求錄用，事下宜州，而知州馮伸己言其妄，編管全州。

translations.literal: Afterward Xifan struck the Denunciation Drum seeking appointment; the matter was sent down to Yizhou, and prefect Feng Shenji said he was presumptuous, and registered him for supervision at Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xifan beat the Denunciation Drum to demand an official post. Yizhou Prefect Feng Shenji called him deluded and had him exiled to Quanzhou under supervision.

sentences.zh: 正辭亦嘗自言功，不報。

translations.literal: Zhengchen also once spoke of his own merit; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen too petitioned for recognition of his service, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 二人皆觖望。

translations.literal: Both men were discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Both men grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 希範後輒遁歸，與正辭率其族人及白崖山酋蒙趕、荔波洞蠻謀為亂，將殺伸己，且曰：「若得廣西一方，當建為大唐國。」

translations.literal: Later Xifan abruptly fled back, and with Zhengchen led his clansmen and Biyai Mountain chieftain Meng Gan and Libo Cave barbarians to plot rebellion, intending to kill Shenji, and saying: "If we obtain one region of Guangxi, we shall establish it as the Great Tang state."
translations.idiomatic: Xifan soon escaped and, with Zhengchen, rallied their clansmen plus Biyai chieftain Meng Gan and the Libo Cave tribes to rebel, planning to kill Feng Shenji and proclaim: "If we seize Guangxi we will restore the Great Tang."

sentences.zh: 會有日者石太清至，因使之筮，太清曰：「君貴不過封侯。」

translations.literal: It happened that diviner Shi Taiqing arrived; they therefore had him cast lots; Taiqing said: "Your nobility will not exceed enfeoffment as marquis."
translations.idiomatic: A fortune-teller named Shi Taiqing was brought in to cast lots. He said, "Your highest rank will be no more than marquis."

sentences.zh: 乃令太清擇日殺牛，建壇場，祭天神，推蒙趕為帝，正辭為奉天開基建國桂王，希範為神武定國令公、桂州牧，皆北向再拜，以為受天命。

translations.literal: They then had Taiqing choose a day to kill an ox, build an altar platform, and sacrifice to heaven; they elevated Meng Gan as emperor, Zhengchen as Fengtian Kaiguo Jianguo Gui King, Xifan as Shenwu Dingguo Commandery Duke and Guilin Prefect—all faced north and bowed twice, taking it as receiving heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: They then had an ox sacrificed on a newly built altar to heaven, proclaimed Meng Gan emperor, Zhengchen as Prince of Gui and founder of the dynasty, and Xifan as Grand Duke and prefect of Guilin—all bowing northward to receive heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 又以區丕績為宰相，餘皆偽立名號，補置四十餘人。

translations.literal: Again they made Qu Piji chancellor; the rest all falsely established titles, appointing more than forty people.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Piji was named chancellor, and more than forty others were given rebel titles and offices.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年正月十三日，率眾五百破環州，劫州印，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the first month of the fourth year of Qingli, leading five hundred masses he broke Huan Prefecture, seized the prefectural seal, and burned its stores.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the first month of Qingli 4 he led five hundred men to seize Huanzhou, steal the prefectural seal, and burn its stores.

sentences.zh: 以環州為武城軍，又破帶溪砦，下鎮寧州及普義砦，有眾一千五百。

translations.literal: He made Huan Prefecture the Wucheng Army, again broke Dai Stream Stockade, took Zhenning Prefecture and Puyi Stockade, and had a host of one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Huanzhou the Wucheng Army, overran Dai Stream Stockade, captured Zhenning Prefecture and Puyi Stockade, and swelled his force to fifteen hundred.

sentences.zh: 宜州捉賊李德用出韓婆嶺擊卻之，前後斬獲甚眾，俘偽將二。

translations.literal: Yizhou bandit-catcher Li Deyong went out through Hanpo Ridge to strike and repel them; before and after, beheadings and captures were very numerous; two false generals were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou's bandit-hunter Li Deyong drove them back at Hanpo Ridge, killing and capturing many and taking two rebel generals prisoner.

sentences.zh: 希範懼，入保荔波洞，間出拒官軍。

translations.literal: Xifan was afraid, entered and held Libo Cave, and intermittently came out to resist official troops.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Xifan withdrew to Libo Cave and only ventured out sporadically to fight government troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷下詔購之，獲希範、正辭及趕者，人賜袍帶、錢三十萬、鹽千斤。

translations.literal: The court issued an edict offering a reward; those who captured Xifan, Zhengchen, and Gan were each granted robes and belts, three hundred thousand cash, and a thousand jin of salt.
translations.idiomatic: The court posted bounties: anyone who captured Xifan, Zhengchen, or Gan received robes, three hundred thousand cash, and a thousand jin of salt.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉運使杜杞大引兵至環州，使攝官區曄、進士曾子華、宜州校吳香誘趕等出降，殺馬牛具酒，紿與之盟，置曼陀羅花酒中，飲者皆昏醉，稍呼起問勞，至則推仆後廡下。

translations.literal: The next year, transport commissioner Du Qi greatly led troops to Huan Prefecture, sending acting official Qu Ye, jinshi Zeng Zihua, and Yizhou sergeant Wu Xiang to lure Gan and others to come out and surrender; they killed horses and cattle and prepared wine, deceiving them into alliance; they placed datura-flower wine in it—those who drank all fell into drunken stupor; gradually calling them up to inquire after their welfare, when they arrived they were pushed down behind the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Transport Commissioner Du Qi marched on Huanzhou and sent Qu Ye, Zeng Zihua, and Wu Xiang to lure Gan and his followers into surrender. At a feast of slaughtered cattle and wine laced with datura, the rebels all fell unconscious and were dragged one by one behind the hall.

sentences.zh: 比暮，眾始覺，驚走，而門有守兵不得出，悉擒之。

translations.literal: By evening the masses at last awoke, fled in alarm, but the gates had guarding troops and they could not get out—all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the rebels roused in panic, but guards blocked the gates and all were seized.

sentences.zh: 後數日，又得希範等，凡獲二百餘人，誅七十八人，餘皆配徙。

translations.literal: Several days later, they again obtained Xifan and others; in all more than two hundred were captured; seventy-eight were executed; the rest were all banished in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Xifan and others were captured as well. More than two hundred rebels were taken; seventy-eight were executed and the rest exiled.

sentences.zh: 仍醢希範，賜諸溪峒，繢其五藏為圖，傳於世，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Still they pickled Xifan and granted him to the various streams and caves; they painted his five viscera as a picture, transmitted through generations; the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xifan's body was pickled and sent to the cave tribes; a painting of his disemboweled organs was circulated as a warning, and the remaining rebels were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 鎮寧州亦隸宜州。

translations.literal: Zhenning Prefecture also was subordinate to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenning Prefecture was also under Yizhou's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，蠻酋莫陵等七百餘人內寇，遣西京作坊使郭誌高、閣門祗候梁紹熙往討，未至，陵等詣桂、宜州巡檢李仲政請降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, barbarian chieftain Mo Ling and more than seven hundred others invaded internally; the court dispatched Western Capital Workshop Commissioner Guo Zhigao and Gate Attendant Liang Shaoxi to go punish them; before they arrived, Ling and others went to Guilin and Yizhou patrol inspector Li Zhongzheng to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 2 more than seven hundred tribesmen under chieftain Mo Ling raided inward. The court sent Workshop Commissioner Guo Zhigao and Gate Attendant Liang Shaoxi to suppress them, but before they arrived Mo Ling and his men surrendered to Patrol Inspector Li Zhongzheng of Guilin and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 廣西轉運使不俟詔，貸其罪。

translations.literal: The Guangxi transport commissioner did not await an edict and pardoned their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for imperial orders, the Guangxi transport commissioner pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 詔劾之，已而釋之。

translations.literal: An edict impeached him, but soon afterward he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The court censured him, yet he was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高、竇州犾獠陳友朋等亦寇海上，本路會兵擊之，潰去。

translations.literal: That year, Chen Youpeng and other tribal leaders of Gao and Dou prefectures also raided the seacoast; troops of this circuit united to attack them, and they scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Chen Youpeng and other tribesmen of Gao and Dou prefectures raided the coast; circuit forces combined against them and drove them off in defeat.
